--- 'Twas the Night Before Madness.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L53
Alessandro Martinez. It was published in the Jesse Dedman William C. Marchese -edited anthology Cthulhu Christmas Special and Other Lovecraftian Yuletide Tales in November 2017. Synopsis The twelve four-line verses describe how, at Christmas time, a cultist conducts a murderous ritual to summon the Old Ones to our plane of existence. As they return to the material realm, they grant him incredible knowledge, but shatter his sanity in the process. Trivia The entities summoned by the cultist include Yog-Sothoth Dagon Hastur Yig Gla'aki Cthulhu Ithaqua Nyarlathotep , and Cthylla


--- 'Umr at-Tawil (Cthulhu Universalis).txt ---

[1] 'Umr at-Tawil L1
НАЗВАНИЕ: 'Umr at-Tawil (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: 'Umr at-Tawil A being who lives in the First Gateway , at the transdimensional extension of earth which is outside time, and serves as a Guide to the next, or Ultimate Gate . 'Umr at-Tawil is the leader of the Ancient Ones (1) , who are manifestations of Yog-Sothoth . 'Umr at-Tawil had been an entity of earth millions of years ago, long before humanity, at the time of the earliest mammals.

[2] 'Umr at-Tawil L23
'Umr at-Tawil is the leader of the Ancient Ones (1) , who are manifestations of Yog-Sothoth . 'Umr at-Tawil had been an entity of earth millions of years ago, long before humanity, at the time of the earliest mammals. 'Umr at-Tawil is heavily cloaked, apparently shaped something like a man, but changeable in shape and half again as large; it moves by gliding or floating.

[3] 'Umr at-Tawil L23
'Umr at-Tawil is the leader of the Ancient Ones (1) , who are manifestations of Yog-Sothoth . 'Umr at-Tawil had been an entity of earth millions of years ago, long before humanity, at the time of the earliest mammals. 'Umr at-Tawil is heavily cloaked, apparently shaped something like a man, but changeable in shape and half again as large; it moves by gliding or floating. The Necronomicon and the Book of Thoth warn of this being, who guides the rash beyond all the worlds into the Abyss of unnameable Devourers. He is known as 'Umr at-Tawil, the Most Ancient One, which the scribe rendereth THE PROLONGED OF LIFE.

[4] 'Umr at-Tawil L31
The Necronomicon and the Book of Thoth warn of this being, who guides the rash beyond all the worlds into the Abyss of unnameable Devourers. He is known as 'Umr at-Tawil, the Most Ancient One, which the scribe rendereth THE PROLONGED OF LIFE. The Necronomicon teaches the obeisances which it is proper to render to 'Umr at-Tawil. He has been feared by the whole world since Lomar rose out of the sea and the Winged Ones came to earth to teach the Elder Lore to man.

[5] 'Umr at-Tawil L55
He knows all things, and He seemed to Randolph Carter to be surprisingly free of the malignity ascribed by Alhazred . 'Umr at-Tawil brandished a large sphere of iridescent metal and led the Ancient Ones in a chanting ritual so that their dreams might open the Ultimate Gate for Carter. 'Umr at-Tawil's magic temporarily hid the revelation of transdimensional selves from Carter while the latter was in the First Gate, so that Carter would be able to use the Silver Key with precision to open the Ultimate Gate.

[2] 'Umr at-Tawil L105
H. P. Lovecraft and E. Hoffmann Price Through the Gates of the Silver Key Umr at-Tawil (عمر الطويل) is a fictional entity from the Cthulhu Mythos . The character was first described by H. P. Lovecraft and E. Hoffmann Price in their short story " Through the Gates of the Silver Key Background 'Umr at-Tawil is an entity who stands beside the Ultimate Gate , meeting any who traverse the first Gate via the Silver Key . He appears as a heavily cloaked figure with no organs or features discernible beneath his garb. It is somewhat humanoid in shape, but "half as large again as an ordinary man", and moves about by gliding or floating over the ground.

[3] 'Umr at-Tawil L135
Abdul Alhazred , in the Necronomicon , identifies this entity as "the Most Ancient One" and "the Prolonged of Life", and cites the Book of Thoth 's claim about a "terrific" price to be paid by those who glimpse at it. Believed to have originated as a prehistoric Earth creature that inhabited the planet long before the dawn of humanity , 'Umr at-Tawil is the leader of the Ancient Ones , which are manifestations of the All-in-One and One-in-All, speculated to be Yog-Sothoth by Randolph Carter HPL Through the Gates of the Silver Key At least one ancient book claimed that 'Umr at-Tawil and the Ancient Ones were agents of Yog-Sothoth, identified as the All-in-One and One-in-All, and that they "dream forever of that time when once again they shall rule to whom rightfully belong Earth and the entire universe of which it is a part".

[4] 'Umr at-Tawil L159
( AWD The House on Curwen Street Pathfinder 'Umr at-Tawil appears as a Great Old One in the role-playing game Pathfinder , under the name Tawil at'Umr In the Pathfinder multiverse, Tawil at'Umr is a servant of Yog-Sothoth, operating as the physical projection of its will and working towards its agenda across the dimensions. Tawil at'Umr is theorized on Golarion to being the side of effect of Yog-Sothoth's contact with the material plane. Its knowledge about reality is vast, including how one may access the Dimension of Time, but one acquires such knowledge at a terrible cost.

[5] Yog-Sothoth L175
Tawil at'Umr is theorized on Golarion to being the side of effect of Yog-Sothoth's contact with the material plane. Its knowledge about reality is vast, including how one may access the Dimension of Time, but one acquires such knowledge at a terrible cost. When it comes to its appearance, mortals see a cloaked humanoid figure which is somewhat larger than the observer.

--- A Colder War.txt ---

[1] The Gate L149
Even Adolf Hitler adhered to the treaty, which hides the existence of the supernatural entities from the public and prohibits their use in war. The United States' countermeasures for Koschei include Project Pluto and a continuity-of-government base hundreds of light years from Earth. American research also indicates that all intelligent species that experiment with the entities exterminate themselves . Other nations emulate the superpowers; Iran and Israel plan a nuclear defense against Ba'athist Iraq's attempts to open a gate to the stars. As a Congressional committee examines the Iran-Contra affair, the Soviets and their leader Yegor Ligachev unexpectedly over-react to a joke by President Reagan, with dire results: Saddam Hussein stabilises the gate of Yog-Sothoth , destroying all opposing tribes in Iraq, to which the Iranians respond by nuking Baghdad; in retaliation, an unknown Russian general launches the entire Russian arsenal aimed at the Middle East; when discussing it with a CIA agent, Oliver North remarks, "Scratch the Middle East, period—everything from the Nile to the Khyber Pass is toast." The escalating nuclear exchange eventually wakes Cthulhu (the actual entity behind Project Koschei ), which shrugs off the entire nuclear arsenal aimed at it and proceeds towards the U. S, annihilating all of Europe in the progress. Information flow across NATO grinds to a halt, as Cthulhu's influence silences and warps all communications. The remaining U. S personnel retreat to a hidden constructed colony on a distant planet, codenamed XK Masada, but are unsure whether they really escaped or are simply enacting a simulation within Cthulhu's mind.

НАЗВАНИЕ: A Handful of Dust ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:11:16 СИМВОЛОВ: 1419 A Handful of Dust Author David Conyers Language English Series Call of Cthulhu Genre(s) Roleplaying game Publisher Yog-Sothoth. com Release Date Preceded by Devil's Children A Handful of Dust: The Witch Cycle Part 2 is a scenario supplement for the Delta Green setting of Chaosium Call of Cthulhu roleplaying game. Written by Australian author and games designer David Conyers , it was published by Call of Cthulhu licensee Yog-Sothoth. com in 2003. Overview Deserts preserve secrets, and the dusty wastelands of New Mexico have buried many. Nearby the test site of the world's first atomic bomb, a centuries-old coven of witches has been resurrected, and Delta Green has been alerted to the emerging threat. Dispatched to the scene, the investigating agents are yet to learn that a far older radioactive horror may overshadow all their expectations.

[4] Yog-Sothoth L77
Dispatched to the scene, the investigating agents are yet to learn that a far older radioactive horror may overshadow all their expectations. Publishers description The story was originally written as a tournament game for the Melbourne, Australia tournament Conquest 1994 , hosted by The Cthulhu Conglomerate. As this predated any mainstream release of Delta Green material (that setting being confined to fanzine releases in The Unspeakable Oath at the time) the original story was devoid of any references to the setting. When it was published in 2003 by Yog-Sothoth. com, the original plot - which involved the players taking part in an FBI investigation - was transplanted into a Delta Green background.

First released as a six-scenario Organized Play series, A Time to Harvest is available now for the first time in a complete and updated tome. The campaign is compatible with both Call of Cthulhu and Pulp Cthulhu rules. The book details the Vermont town, helping you bring it to life at the tabletop, and to give the setting for your games of Call of Cthulhu a rich, lived-in feeling. --- Alien (franchise).txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L89
The series has also crossed over with other popular properties, including The Terminator Marvel Comics The Avengers Vampirella Judge Dredd , D. C. Comics' Batman and Superman Buffy the Vampire Slayer , and Predator . The latter, launched in 1990 by Dark Horse Comics in Dark Horse Presents and supported by an Easter egg in the film Predator 2 the same year, has established itself as a long-term interaction between the two properties. Although featuring little in the way of specific references to either the works of H. P. Lovecraft or the Cthulhu Mythos in general, the Alien franchise was intended to have a more direct connection from its inception, with writer Dan O'Bannon's early screenplay showing the titular aliens as having a connection to the Outer God Yog-Sothoth Despite this having been written out in the final draft, the finished film has been cited as a prime example of cosmic horror in cinema, Elements and Themes Central to the franchise's stories are the titular aliens, most commonly referred to as Xenomorphs since the release of the first sequel film, Aliens , in 1986. These creatures are multi-stage, insect-like parasitic lifeforms which require a living host in which to gestate; birth invariably results in the death of the host. The Xenomorphs are highly-aggressive, lethal predators who will do anything to protect their hive colonies, and possess a defence mechanism in the form of acid blood, meaning that even in death, a Xenomorph has the potential to eliminate its opponent.

They seem to be heavily cloaked, with some neutral-coloured fabric, without eye-holes. Upon their cloaked heads rest tall, uncertainly coloured mitres. Grasped in certain folds of their swathings are long sceptres with carven heads. And Randolph Carter The Ancient Ones welcomed Randolph Carter, "whose daring has made you one of us." A vacant pedestal was reserved for him. Under 'Umr at-Tawil's guidance, they dreamed on Carter's behalf, while they swayed gently and light emanated from their heads. Their dreams opened the Ultimate Gate so that Carter could pass through and meet Yog-Sothoth. Their Origin It seems likely that the Ancient Ones were earthly mortals who were promoted to their current state by Yog-Sothoth. For Yog-Sothoth said that he had shown the Ultimate Mystery only eleven times to beings of Earth, of which only five were human or human-like.

Все книги до единой, включая "Анналы Юга", исчезли навеки. Людей пробрала дрожь от спокойного, задумчивого тона Горты. В мире, где книги переписывались от руки монахами, пропали тысячи часов труда. Остальные тут же вскочили, помогая грузить провизию и затягивая подпруги. Лидия вернулась от реки и убрала свои немногие пожитки в сумку.

В воздухе висел запах плесени. Он осторожно приоткрыл дверь. Горта изумленно уставился внутрь. Наконец-то она была здесь, прямо перед ним, и он вот-вот откроет ее страницы и впитает подробности своего будущего. Сердце его тоскливо сжалось при мысли броситься назад и показать книгу Лидии. Горта протянул руку. В тот же миг лунный свет, струившийся из окон коридора, исчез. Все небо потемнело за считанные секунды. Отряд погрузился в черноту. Горта приказал всем стоять тихо и не двигаться. Воины ждали его следующей команды. В тишине внезапно поднялся ветер, завывая вокруг древних башен города. Тьма сгущалась, пока Горта не перестал видеть собственную руку перед лицом. Он протянул руку к обшитым вишневыми панелями стенам и попытался понемногу отступать обратно в том направлении, откуда они пришли. Он приказал остальным делать то же самое.

--- Anubis (Cthulhu Universalis).txt ---

[1] The Opener of the Way L61
An Egyptian cult of priest-sorcerers viewed their gods, including Anubis, as the representatives of actual Hidden Beings—monstrous beast-men who shambled on Earth in primal days [ RB Fane ]. According to the Daemonolorum there was a sect of Egypt which believed that their gods, including Anubis, could assume human form [ RB Brood ]. According to Saracenic Rituals , Anubis was one of a number of strange hybrids who walked the earth when it was young; gigantic, lumbering creatures-half-beast, half-man [ RB Sebek ]. Anubis is the Opener of the Way, jackal-headed god who guards cryptic Karneter, and holds the keys to Life and Death. He is not a friend of those who rule. He stands in shadows, for he is the Keeper of Mysteries. It is written that an evil priest called the Master carved the first statue of the true form of Anubis; and that the statue now guards the Master's tomb. Archeologists Ronald Barton and Peter Barton discovered the tomb and found two images of Anubis. The first was a silver symbol on a door, with the heads of seven principal Egyptian gods: Osiris Isis Ra Bast Thoth Set , and Anubis.

However, his body died in the process. When his grief-stricken son Peter assaulted the statue, it slew him. [ RB Opener The Probilski Foundation had a statue of jackal-headed Anubis. --- Archetypes (Cthulhu Universalis).txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L7
НАЗВАНИЕ: Archetypes (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Archetypes Archetypes (1, of Yog-Sothoth) HPL Gates online text )]: People of the ultimate abyss, with an infinite number of dimensions, or perhaps existing outside all dimensions. They are "prodigious forms whose multiple extensions transcended any conception of being, size, and boundaries." They exist outside of time with no past, present, or future. Individuals in our world are each three-dimensional cross sections of one or another of the archetypes. Cross sections of the same archetype at different angles correspond to different individuals. Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L27
НАЗВАНИЕ: Archetypes (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Archetypes Archetypes (1, of Yog-Sothoth) HPL Gates online text )]: People of the ultimate abyss, with an infinite number of dimensions, or perhaps existing outside all dimensions. They are "prodigious forms whose multiple extensions transcended any conception of being, size, and boundaries." They exist outside of time with no past, present, or future. Individuals in our world are each three-dimensional cross sections of one or another of the archetypes. Cross sections of the same archetype at different angles correspond to different individuals. Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype. Slight changes of the angle of a slice can also correspond to different stages in the life of a single individual, such as Randolph Carter. Of all the archetypes, Yog-Sothoth is supreme, and is the source of "all great wizards, all great thinkers, all great artists" on every world. Lovecraft and his coauthor, E. Hoffman Price, do not provide any information about the other archetypes. Since Yog-Sothoth is an archetype, it is conceivable that some of Lovecraft's other major beings are also archetypes.

[3] Yog-Sothoth L29
They exist outside of time with no past, present, or future. Individuals in our world are each three-dimensional cross sections of one or another of the archetypes. Cross sections of the same archetype at different angles correspond to different individuals. Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype. Slight changes of the angle of a slice can also correspond to different stages in the life of a single individual, such as Randolph Carter. Of all the archetypes, Yog-Sothoth is supreme, and is the source of "all great wizards, all great thinkers, all great artists" on every world. Lovecraft and his coauthor, E. Hoffman Price, do not provide any information about the other archetypes. Since Yog-Sothoth is an archetype, it is conceivable that some of Lovecraft's other major beings are also archetypes. For example, Azathoth could be an archetype of dreamers or creators, Nyarlathotep could be the archetypal messenger, and Shub-Niggurath could be an archetype of fertility. The Other Gods could all be archetypes, or they could all be cross-sections of Azathoth. Cthulhu could be the archetype of priests.

[4] Yog-Sothoth L31
Examples are Randolph Carter and the wizard Zkauba , who dwell in different solar systems, but who are both slices of the Yog-Sothoth archetype. Slight changes of the angle of a slice can also correspond to different stages in the life of a single individual, such as Randolph Carter. Of all the archetypes, Yog-Sothoth is supreme, and is the source of "all great wizards, all great thinkers, all great artists" on every world. Lovecraft and his coauthor, E. Hoffman Price, do not provide any information about the other archetypes. Since Yog-Sothoth is an archetype, it is conceivable that some of Lovecraft's other major beings are also archetypes. For example, Azathoth could be an archetype of dreamers or creators, Nyarlathotep could be the archetypal messenger, and Shub-Niggurath could be an archetype of fertility. The Other Gods could all be archetypes, or they could all be cross-sections of Azathoth. Cthulhu could be the archetype of priests. It is a disturbing cosmology, since it implies that we are each derived from one of these unspeakably alien beings, or at least that we have a common source with them. No information is presented about the appearance of these archetypes.

Overview The Second Edition Core Set had been quite drastically overhauled from the First Edition, with many major changes such as the removal of randomised movement rates and the addition of Ancient Ones to serve as final "bosses" for the Investigators. These entities increased the difficulty of the game by a large factor, but a confrontation could be avoided if the players closed all open portals on the board within a certain time limit. It was also the first edition to be supplied with expansion packs, add-ons which featured additional equipment, skills, spells, encounters, Investigators and Ancient Ones, to play with, with most featuring optional game mechanics to change the way the core set is played, and a handful even containing additional game boards to expand the area of action beyond Arkham List of Expansions The Curse of the Dark Pharaoh The Dunwich Horror Deluxe Expansion The King in Yellow Kingsport Horror Deluxe Expansion The Black Goat of the Woods Innsmouth Horror Deluxe Expansion The Lurker at the Threshold Miskatonic Horror Deluxe Expansion Characters Included Ancient Ones Azathoth Cthulhu Hastur Ithaqua Nyarlathotep Shub-Niggurath Yig Yog-Sothoth Investigators "Ashcan" Pete , the Drifter Amanda Sharpe , the Student Bob Jenkins , the Salesman Carolyn Fern , the Psychologist Darrell Simmons , the Photographer Dexter Drake , the Magician Gloria Goldberg , the Author Harvey Walters , the Professor Jenny Barnes , the Dilettante Joe Diamond , the Private Eye Kate Winthrop , the Scientist Mandy Thompson , the Researcher Michael McGlen , the Gangster Monterey Jack , the Archaeologist Sister Mary , the Nun Vincent Lee , the Doctor Monsters Included The Black Man The Bloated Woman Byakhee Chthonian Cultist Dark Pharaoh Dark Young Dhole Dimensional Shambler Elder Thing Fire Vampire Flying Polyps Formless Spawn Ghost Ghoul God of the Bloody Tongue Gug The Haunter of the Dark High Priest Hound of Tindalos Maniac Mi-Go Nightgaunt Star-Spawn Shoggoth Vampire Warlock Witch Zombie

НАЗВАНИЕ: Arkham: Reanimated ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:11:57 СИМВОЛОВ: 6166 Arkham: Reanimated Author Brandon Berntson Country United States Language English Series The Lovecraft Mysteries Release Date February 2020 Pages Preceded by The Night of Dagon Followed by The Lurker at the Threshold Arkham: Reanimated is a Cthulhu Mythos novel by American author Brandon Berntson , the second in his Lovecraft Mysteries series. Running to a total of 168 pages, it was independently published in February 2020; both paperback and digital editions were released. Synopsis Millie Von Clydesburgh and Devlin Macky decide to take a day trip to the countryside, but become stranded in the near-derelict tumbledown that is Arkham . There, they encounter hostile locals, reanimated corpses , abominable experiments, and even an Outer God in their efforts to find out what secrets haunt the mysterious town.

--- August Derleth_ posthumous collaboration controversy.txt ---

[1] The Lurker at the Threshold L55
P. Lovecraft and August Derleth," were in fact written almost entirely by Derleth. In most cases, the stories were based on one or more ideas noted in Lovecraft’s Commonplace Book ; for example, "The Fisherman of Falcon Point" was based on this entry: "Fisherman casts his net into the sea by moonlight—what he finds." Plotting, description, dialogue, characterization, and other elements were entirely by Derleth. As such they cannot be classified as works by Lovecraft. In some instances Derleth incorporated actual prose passages by Lovecraft into his stories. The Lurker at the Threshold (a 50,000-word novel) contains about 1,200 words by Lovecraft, most of it taken from a fragment entitled "Of Evill Sorceries Done in New England" (see B-i-42), the balance from a fragment now titled "The Rose Window" (see B-ii-322). "The Survivor" was based on a comparatively lengthy plot sketch plus random notes for the story jotted down by Lovecraft in 1934. A descriptive passage of "The Lamp of Alhazred" was based on a portion of a letter by Lovecraft to Derleth, 18 November 1936. These extracts or paraphrases, however, have not been deemed significant enough to merit inclusion in this bibliography. The 16 Stories The 16 stories that S. T.

[2] The Lurker at the Threshold L63
"The Survivor" was based on a comparatively lengthy plot sketch plus random notes for the story jotted down by Lovecraft in 1934. A descriptive passage of "The Lamp of Alhazred" was based on a portion of a letter by Lovecraft to Derleth, 18 November 1936. These extracts or paraphrases, however, have not been deemed significant enough to merit inclusion in this bibliography. The 16 Stories The 16 stories that S. T. Joshi has separated apart, which have been in the past uncritically attributed to both Lovecraft and Derleth as co-authors, or even to Lovecraft alone, are: The Lurker at the Threshold (1945) The Survivor " (1954) The Ancestor " (1957) The Gable Window " (1957) The Lamp of Alhazred " (1957) The Peabody Heritage " (1957) The Shadow Out of Space " (1957) Wentworth's Day " (1957) The Fisherman of Falcon Point " (1959) The Shuttered Room " (1959) Witches' Hollow " (1962) The Shadow in the Attic " (1964) The Dark Brotherhood " (1966) The Horror from the Middle Span " (1974) Innsmouth Clay " (1974) The Watchers Out of Time " (1974, unfinished before Derleth's death in 1971) S. T. Joshi's scholarship confirmed what was known privately for many years, that none of the above works are by H. P. Lovecraft. All of them are properly to be considered entirely the works of August Derleth. This has no relevancy to any praise or criticism of these stories based on their merits; this is a matter completely related to authorship alone. Posthumous Collaboration: A Mythos Tradition?

--- Averoigne.txt ---

[1] Iog-Sotôt L75
The fictional land appears to based on the historical province of Auvergne. The frequent references to Lovecraftian deities, often in transparently altered terms (Sodaqui for Tsathoggua , Iog-Sotôt for Yog-Sothoth , the Ram With a Thousand Ewes for Shub-Niggurath ), establish Averoigne as a part of the Cthulhu Mythos In addition to Mythos entities and their worshippers, Smith populates Averoigne with malign and dangerous creatures like vampires Rendezvous in Averoigne lamias The End of the Story ", possibly " The Enchantress of Sylaire "), and satyrs The Satyr Stories Smith used Averoigne as the setting for the following stories: The End of the Story Weird Tales , May 1930) A Rendezvous in Averoigne Weird Tales , April/May 1931) The Satyr La Paree Stories , July 1931) The Maker of Gargoyles Weird Tales , August 1932) The Mandrakes Weird Tales , February 1933) The Beast of Averoigne Weird Tales , May 1933) The Holiness of Azédarac Weird Tales , November 1933) The Colossus of Ylourgne Weird Tales , June 1934) The Disinterment of Venus Weird Tales , July 1934) Mother of Toads Weird Tales , July 1938) The Enchantress of Sylaire Weird Tales , July 1941) Averoigne " (poetry) ( Challenge , Spring 1951) These stories are collected in The Averoigne Archives: The Complete Averoigne Tales of Clark Ashton Smith , an ebook published by Pickman's Press in 2019. Geography Smith places Averoigne near the center of France, in the highland region known as the Central Massif. The northern half of the territory is dominated by the walled city of Vyônes , site of an impressive cathedral. In the southern half is located the town of Ximes. The main road of Averoigne runs between Ximes and Vyônes, straight through the thick, dark forest that blankets the province.

--- Basalt Pillars of the West.txt ---

[1] The Gate L45
НАЗВАНИЕ: Basalt Pillars of the West ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:12:22 СИМВОЛОВ: 1068 Basalt Pillars of the West Location The Dreamlands Type Gate First appearance HPL The White Ship Appearances HPL The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath Created by H. P. Lovecraft The Basalt Pillars of the West are a pair of pillars of gargantuan size made of basalt (a dark volcanic rock) that rise from the ocean in the Dreamlands on the western edge of the world. The pillars form the gate of a monstrous cataract whose swift, resistless waters spill over the edge into the "abysmal nothingness" of planetary space. The pillars are shrouded in mist so that none may see beyond them until one sails through the pillars and the mists are lifted, at which point the current becomes too strong to escape. ( HPL The White Ship HPL The Dream-Quest of Unknown Kadath Basil Elton sailed through the Basalt Pillars aboard the White Ship on his search for the fabled land of Cathuria but never found it.

--- Billington House (Cthulhu Universalis).txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L59
In between the house and the tower is a marsh with frogs and whippoorwills that signal when the servants of the Great Old Ones (3) are present. In 1921, family descendant Ambrose Dewart decided to move into the old house and restore it. Stephen Bates visited him there later. Dr. Seneca Lapham inferred that an influence was being exercised on the inhabitants of Billington House. With the help of Winfield Phillips , Dr. Lapham was able to kill Richard Billington (who had possessed the body of Ambrose Dewart) and Quamis before they could finish summoning Yog-Sothoth into our world via a ritual at the stone tower. The location of Billington House is a bit difficult to visualize. The opening paragraphs of AWD Lurker seem to give the impression that Billington House is a short distance off the Aylesbury Pike as you proceed northwest from Arkham in the direction of Dunwich . From this, you might expect Dunwich to be somewhere to the northwest of Billington House. However, Laban Billington , when he lived at Billington House, heard cries "east by northeast, which is the direction of Dunwich, or the wild country around Dunwich."

НАЗВАНИЕ: Black Tallow ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:12:39 СИМВОЛОВ: 1265 Black Tallow Author Edward M. Erdelac Language English Genre(s) Horror Publisher April Moon Books Publication The Dark Rites of Cthulhu Publication date March 2014 Black Tallow " is a short Cthulhu Mythos story by American author Edward M. Erdelac Synopsis When Raymond, a specialist in translating ancient texts, is contacted by his old friend Paul, a successful businessman who wishes to pay him seven million dollars to translate a ritualistic text, he jumps at the chance. However, while translating the text at Paul's house, Raymond slowly comes to the realisation that in preparation for enacting the ritual - which he believes will allow him to commune with Yog-Sothoth and Azathoth amongst others, and grant him ultimate knowledge of the universe - Paul has murdered his wife and daughter, and rendered them down into tallow for devotional candles. In the meantime, Paul takes the translation but imperfectly completes the rite, and is consumed by an entity from beyond. Characters Raymond , a scholarly but poor man in his middle age. Paul Woodson , Raymond's former college roommate, now head of a successful multinational. "Black Tallow" was published in the Brian M. Sammons -edited anthology The Dark Rites of Cthulhu by April Moon Books in March 2014.

--- Blessed of Shub-Niggurath.txt ---

[1] The Gate L129
When completed, the ritual tears the fabric of space allowing travel between distant places, much like a temporary Gate spell. A group of gof ’nn hupadgh gather in a circle and begin to chant. Each sacrifices a point of power while their leader offers a blood sacrifice to Shub-Niggurath—the sacrifice may be a cow, one or more humans, or several smaller animals. In particularly auspicious times, the gof ’nn hupadgh may sacrifice one or more of their own. As the blood soaks into the ground, a scarlet circle appears—the Gate. The gof ’nn hupadgh may go through the portal or they may summon some portion or herald of Shub-Niggurath to come through to them. The gof ’nn hupadgh have complete control of where the Gate opens. The temporary Gate lasts for 12 seconds per point of power sacrificed by the group. Summary The Blessed are a mutant race created by Shub-Niggurath to be its priests and servants. They were human sacrifices it swallowed which were later "born" from its body, having been greatly mutated.

Again she shook her head and laying a finger to her lips cautiously, she beckoned me to look through the door by which I'd entered. The gate opening into the garden from the courtyard was partly open. What I seen made my hair stand up. It was nearly dark. The garden looked shadowy and mysterious, but it was still light enough for me to make out the figgers of five big coolies sneaking along with long curved knives in their hands. "They look for you," whispered the girl. "Tung Yin fear spies. They know somebody climb the wall. Wait, we hide you."

"Don't worry." She smiled. "I can handle Tung Yin. Go now, please. And thank you." Well, she turned and went on in the house. We listened a minute and heard somebody howling and cussing in Chinese, and knowed Tung Yin had come to. We was fixing to go in and rescue Miss Worley, when we heard her talking to him, sharp and hard-like. He quieted down purty quick, so we looked at each other plumb mystified, and went on out in the garden and found the gate Bill come in at and went through it. We hadn't gone but a few yards when Bill says: "Dern it, Steve, I've lost that pipe I took offa Tung Yin." "Well, gee whiz," I said disgustedly. "You ain't goin' back to look for it." --- Brown Jenkin.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L93
H. P. Lovecraft The Dreams in the Witch-House When Walter Gilman managed to kill Mason, Jenkin replied in kind by burrowing though his chest and eating his heart. Brown Jenkin's bones were later found with those of Mason and several small children by workers tearing out a slanting wall. Behind the Mythos The origins of Brown Jenkin are subject to debate. Perhaps the most popular theory is that he is the child of Keziah and Nyarlathotep , the Lovecraftian deity she presumably serves. This is rather likely, considering that Lavinia Whateley mated with Yog-Sothoth , and that in The Lurker at the Threshold (posthumously published and co-written with August Derleth ) there is a quote that reads: "'She affirm'd, and her good neighbours likewise, that it had been borne to her, and took oath that she did not know by what manner it had come upon her, for it was neither Beast nor Man but like to a monstrous Bat with human face.'" Another theory, proposed by Weird Tales columnist Kenneth Hite , is that Brown Jenkin was a higher dimensional servitor of Nyarlathotep who was rewarded as being a familiar. However, as he was in the third dimension, he could only appear as a third-dimensional interpretation of what he was (this being similar to the vistas of Hyperspace in the story).

He is expected one day to awake and eat up the world. They have no religion beyond those gloomy dreams." [Australia, Encyclopædia Britannica, Ninth Edition, v. 3, p. 113. Thanks to Michael Bukowski for publicizing this quote on yog-blogsoth. blogspot. com (retrieved 07/08/2024).] "The Turrabool speaking aborigines who inhabited the district of the Upper Brisbane River, in South Queensland, had a tradition regarding a spirit or unseen Being whom they called Budjali. This being was called Buddai (Buddha 1) by another tribe. They believed him to be the common ancestor of their race, and described him as an old man of great stature. They stated that he had been lying asleep for ages with his head leaning on one arm , and the arm buried deep in the sand.

--- CTHULHU_IN_MESOAMERICA_69595b8a1c.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L31
Huitzilopochtli was the patron god of the Aztecs who led them to the "promised land," the island in the center of Lake Tenochtitlan where they founded a capital, much as Yahweh led the Hebrews to Canaan. He has nothing to do with water or "Deep Ones" -- he seems primarily a war god -- again like Yahweh -- and he was born of a virgin-mother goddess. Perhaps the final letters of his name, "chtli," have something to do with Laney's correlation. At any rate, he would seem to be more likely one of the spawn of Yog-Sothoth, who is know to beget his progeny on mankind ... But in "The Mound" we read that the humans who occupy blue-litten K'n-yan, which land lies somewhere far within the earth beneath the southwestern United States, carried on trade or contact of some sort with the surface Indians of centuries ago. The people of K'n-yan worshipped Yig and Cthulhu, and their images often occupied the same temple. Furthermore, it is definitely stated that Yig is the prototype of the great Mesoamerican god Quetzalcoatl, the "feathered serpent."

Collection By 1931 the Hall of Mummies on the second floor of the West Wing is said to be the finest collection of its kind in America, housing: Egyptian Mummies from Early Sakkarah through to the 8th century Coptic period. Prehistoric Indian examples from the Aleutian Islands. Several petrified citizens from the ruins of Pompeii. "Natural" mummies from people trapped in mines around the world. The mummy of T'yog , which entered the collection in November 1879. Preserved bodies from the crypts of Château Fausses-flammes in Averoigne , France, obtained in Spring 1931. The Museum also has a basement library of books on lost cultures that also contains T'yog's scroll. Staff Curator Pickman - The curator in 1879. Richard H. Johnson Ph. In theory, it means a body of work that an established body of literature that can draw upon, but it is more commonly thought as what a fan considers what forms part of the Mythos, or what "really happened."

[3] The Key L151
This is to say, each main character/narrator (many of which assert their unreliability) is at best partially correct, and the information they acquire in the course of their uncanny experiences is of even lesser reliability. Lovecraft reminds us that we cannot understand the universe as it is, and perhaps gives us the key to the "harmony" of the Mythos: it is only discord. However, it is the opinion of most current Lovecraft scholars, and of this wiki, that the closer one comes to the original Lovecraft Myth Cycle, the closer to the "truth" one gets.

[4] Yog-Sothothery L167
There are discussion about what was intended as being part of the Mythos or not since he did not make a list for a collection publication while alive. In his letters,he referred to a story of this kind as a "Yog-Sothothery" and to refer to the whole as the "Arkham cycle" (specifically stating "The Colour out of Space" and "The Dunwich Horror" to be part of it). This terms are hard to use since the first would exclude stories which don't have the Great Elder themselves and the second one would exclude stories which don't take place in Arkham (such as "The Call of Cthulhu") but would include stories that could seem unrelated (such as "Herbert West--Reanimator").

--- Carl Sanford.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L45
НАЗВАНИЕ: Carl Sanford ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:13:06 СИМВОЛОВ: 2070 Carl Sanford Also known as Carl Sandford Origin Unknown, possibly Arkham Powers and Abilities Extensive Spellcasting Abilities Extensive Occult Knowledge Occupation Antiquarian Affiliations The Silver Twilight Lodge Species Human Appearances EXP Shadows of Yog-Sothoth Masks of Nyarlathotep Feeders from Within Carl Sanford is a fictional character from the expanded Cthulhu Mythos . He appears in Chaosium Call of Cthulhu role-playing game, and in Fantasy Flight Games Arkham Horror Files -related content. Description The High Priest of Arkham Silver Twilight Lodge , Sanford is a tall, slim man with an air of breeding about him. An antiquarian by trade, he holds a degree of influence in nearly every organisation in the city. Despite his standing in the community, there are many who fear the man, and rumours abound regarding the unwholesome deeds perpetrated in both his name and that of the Lodge.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L87
He appears in Chaosium Call of Cthulhu role-playing game, and in Fantasy Flight Games Arkham Horror Files -related content. Description The High Priest of Arkham Silver Twilight Lodge , Sanford is a tall, slim man with an air of breeding about him. An antiquarian by trade, he holds a degree of influence in nearly every organisation in the city. Despite his standing in the community, there are many who fear the man, and rumours abound regarding the unwholesome deeds perpetrated in both his name and that of the Lodge. Call of Cthulhu RPG Sanford was first introduced in Shadows of Yog-Sothoth as the central antagonist, working behind the scenes of the Order of the Silver Twilight, and using other "Lords of the Silver Twilight" to raise the island of R'lyeh and possibly to even wake Cthulhu , depending on the player's intervention. Canonically, this fails, but Sanford escapes and then reappears in Masks of Nyarlathotep as a secondary antagonist in the China chapter. In Cults of Cthulhu , he is listed as an example "Deathless Master" (a leader of the global Cthulhu cult , coequal to the "deathless Chinaman" of The Call of Cthulhu , whom the book names Hui Qiang), or maybe even a direct agent of Cthulhu, but the book leaves the exact interpretation up to the Keeper.

--- Castles of Circles [Перевод [Перевод.txt].txt].txt ---

[1] Той L31
Я вызывал демонов и получше, чем вы, бездушные людишки." Он обратил свой взор на Пферзонна. "Вставай, ты, и убери этот беспорядок — или пеняй на себя." Волшебник приказал слугам принести еду для своих не самых желанных гостей и поручил другому тщательно вычистить пол в комнате, где он позволил ворам спать, оставив починку потолка на более позднее время дня. Волшебник Умма Зата, более известный просто под своей фамилией, вызволил Пферзонна и Вальзарума, заплатив тюремщику штраф, который они навлекли на себя в результате своей последней неудачной выходки. Не то чтобы они были некомпетентными преступниками, просто невезучими, и Зата полагал, что их невезение изменится или, по крайней мере, даст готовое оправдание их неудаче в осуществлении той схемы, которую он для них задумал. В любом случае, чувствовал он, он в выигрыше. Он получит желаемое или же предоставит подходящую жертву для младшего бога. Что касается двух воров, у них были свои собственные идеи. За столом они обедали редкими зверями. Зата любил откармливать свою добычу. Он внимательно слушал план воров по осуществлению его предложения, не будучи полностью уверенным в его успехе, но снова думая о преимуществе, которое можно извлечь даже из возможной неудачи. Он всё же не смог удержаться от комментария. "Клянусь туманами тёмных гор, я понятия не имею, что сказать на ваши предложения."

[3] Той L83
К несчастью, Пферзонну пришлось учитывать реальность их нынешнего положения. Наблюдая, как Зата жадно глотает из своего кубка, он знал, что у него нет иного выбора, кроме как идти с ним в предложенной им схеме. Все прочие личности в городе были ещё более одиозными и ненадёжными, чем толстый волшебник, сидевший перед ним, и, вероятно, предлагали сделки похуже. Для них не было альтернативы в этом городе джунглей. Только юг Гипербореи сулил, вероятно, лучший шанс, но им нужны были деньги, чтобы туда добраться. Это последнее воровское дело и было той возможностью, если они преуспеют. Пферзонн вздохнул и уставился на свои ногти, размышляя, как убедить Вальзарума в том, что они приняли правильное решение, прибегнув к руководству Заты. Горячие свежие булочки, принесённые к столу трактирной служанкой, были приятны на вкус. Вальзарум с удовольствием жевал хлеб, наблюдая, как Пферзонн спорит о счёте с трактирщиком. Наконец он произнёс: "Я искренне надеюсь, что Зата не погубит наше дело из-за этих дурацких мелочей." "Согласен. Или не убьёт нас каким-нибудь особенно ужасным образом.

[4] Тот L109
Вальзарум вздохнул и запихнул в рот ещё одну булочку. "Он волшебник, и у него есть свои способы всё выведать, — сказал он. — После этого нам нужно покинуть город." "Он не всемогущ, Валь. Он не может починить собственную крышу", — заметил Пферзонн. "Итак, мы отправимся в этот Замок Кругов, чтобы добыть Книгу Эйбона для человека, который никудышный хозяин?" "Не просто книгу. Подлинную рукопись с его аннотированными заметками. Это мечта каждого некроманта и волшебника в этой земле." "Я думал, старый Эйбон забрал её с собой, когда исчез в своём зеркале." "Не тот фолиант, что нужен Зате." "Он платит нам достаточно, чтобы уехать из Узулдарума, — сказал Вальзарум. Снова вздохнув, он добавил: — Мне так сильно хочется на юг. Я скучаю по дому." Ло Пферзонн посмотрел на него с лёгкой грустью. Узулдарум был всем, что он знал, но у каждого города своё время, и он знал, что его время в этом городе прошло. Мужчины пробирались по улицам ночного города, выбирая задворки рыночного квартала Узулдарума, старейшего района, оставшегося относительно нетронутым со времен его заселения.

[5] Тот L157
Это была та самая подлинная рукопись, написанная Эйбоном, со всеми заметками и комментариями, которые Зата помогал ему делать, будучи учеником, и заполненная разделами, которые легендарный некромант позже отбросил при завершении своей книги. Пферзонн потянулся к ней и вытащил её с места, после чего был выдернут из пространства и растянулся на полу. Горго выхватил книгу из его рук и передал своему хозяину. Умма Зата прижал книгу к груди, словно первенца. Волшебник стоял молча, пока Пферзонн поднимался с пола. Всё ещё прижимая книгу, Зата произнёс: "А теперь — принесём жертву." Инстинктивно Вальзарум потянулся к своему мечу, но Горго схватил его за руку, прежде чем тот успел вынуть клинок из ножен. Пока они боролись, Зата начал читать заклинание. Вальзарум лягнул ногой и сбил Горго с ног. Оба мужчины были одинакового размера, но Горго легко упал. Он рухнул в трапециевидную выемку и застрял в полу, не в силах пошевелиться. Он начал кричать. Заклинание, наложенное Затой для открытия пространства, закрывалось, и гранитный пол возвращался на место, безжалостно дробя его, рассекая тело на уровне пояса и коленей. Оба вора отпрянули, а Зата продолжал читать заклинание, игнорируя последние исполненные ужаса мгновения своего слуги. Вальзарум выхватил меч и начал отступать от волшебника.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L57
P. Lovecraft 's " The Dunwich Horror Background The Children of Yog-Sothoth are mortal creatures infused with the Outer God Yog-Sothoth 's essence. Most of them can pass for a prominent member of a specific species (relating to the mother) if they wear clothing that hides the monstrous elements in its body. These features include tentacles, eyes, and tails, along with extra maws in places where joints or vertebrae would be expected.

[3] Yog-Sothoth L63
They are not born evil and have complex morals, but since nearly all of them are raised by the cults that create them, they almost always have evil tendencies manifesting in passive malevolence in the good of their respective cult group. Creating a Child of Yog-Sothoth involves a blasphemous ritual in which a humanoid or animal is used as an incubator, the child's seed combined with the blood of a member in a pact of Yog-Sothoth. The mother dies upon giving birth and usually gives birth to twins, a Child of Yog-Sothoth and a Spawn of Yog-Sothoth . If twins are not produced, the offspring are still birthed.

[4] Yog-Sothoth L63

--- Chorazos Cult.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L19
НАЗВАНИЕ: Chorazos Cult ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:13:23 СИМВОЛОВ: 1332 The Chorazos Cult (erroneously called " Choronzon Cult ") is a religious cult dedicated to the worship of Yog-Sothoth . It appears in the Encyclopedia Cthulhiana , a supplement to the role-playing game Call of Cthulhu . The cult gets its name from the founder, a man of supposed gypsy descent who welcomed cultists from various parts of the world. This enigmatic and fanatical cult was founded in the mountains of Romania in the late 16th century, but moved to Elizabethan England. Although they owned a temple in Finchley with royal approval, an investigation by John Dee forced them to leave the place.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L33
It was then that they settled in a house, but a year later the locals set it on fire, with which they cursed the place and left. It was then that Chorazos and his followers arrived in Scotland. Although King James IV opposed what he saw as witchcraft, the cult developed a good reputation due to its alleged healing powers, but was eventually disbanded again by the villagers as its true nature was revealed. The cult returned to the present day in the United States. Its goal is to awaken Yog-Sothoth. Curiosities The name of this fanatic cult could be an allusion to Choronzon, a demon that appears in the writings of the occultists John Dee and Edward Kelley, and that again would be referenced in those of Aleister Crowley.

It all had a desolate and forbidding air; and I felt in my very marrow the brooding chillness that had come in from the unseen marsh in that dismal, ever-coiling fog. But the light was promise of human nearness on the lonely downs; and I might obtain shelter for the night, or at least find someone who could direct me to a town or inn. Somewhat to my surprise, the gate was unlocked. It swung inward with a rusty grating sound, as if it had not been opened for a long time; and pushing my motorcycle before me, I followed a weed-grown drive toward the light. The rambling mass of a large manor-house disclosed itself, among trees and shrubs whose artificial forms, like the hedge of ragged yew, were assuming a wilder grotesquery than they had received from the hand of the topiary. The fog had turned into a bleak drizzle.

--- Clavicle_of_Nyarlathotep_(Cthulhu_Universalis)_e3bbf64102.txt ---

[1] The Key L19
Источник (URL): Название: Clavicle of Nyarlathotep (Cthulhu Universalis) Автор: Unknown Источник данных: live-сайт Символов: 706 Сохранено: 2026-08-25T21:58:32+03:00 SHA-256 контента: cae8615bc2602aa1c3decf0a2dc7417f16229c0d9d03cce79a1409ad14a7bd72 ТЕКСТ Clavicle of Nyarlathotep Georg Reuter Fischer heard voices mention the clavicle of Nyarlathotep as part of a list of books [FL Terror2]. In this case, "clavicle" is probably not a reference to a collarbone, but is used like the Latin word Clavicula, meaning a key. The title is reminiscent of the Key of Solomon (Latin: Clavicula Salomonis), a Renaissance-era book of magic that was misleadingly attributed to the Biblical King Solomon. One can surmise that the Clavicle of Nyarlathotep is a Renaissance-era book of spells that are attributed to Nyarlathotep. When originally issued, the book may have had a Latin title like Clavicula Niarlathotepus. Return to Cthulhu Universalis Contents Page

В такие места тянулись твари, одни — природные, другие — нет. Харкан знал не понаслышке, что есть падальщики и хищники, питающиеся не только кровью и плотью. --- Concerning Rudolf Hess, Mr Buckle and the Book.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L77
Synopsis During the Second World War, James Worth, a highly skilled thief, is released early from prison by Mr. Buckle, a representative of the War Office, in exchange for the return of an item he stole from a British Museum storage warehouse: a copy of the infamous Necronomicon Worth soon comes to realise, however, that Mr. Buckle is not at all what he seems, and sets about the business of retrieving the cursed book. Tracking the man to a secret location deep beneath the streets of London, he thwarts a ritual to Yog-Sothoth being conducted by Buckle and his cronies. The group are seemingly destroyed by the Outer God in the city sewers. Behind the Mythos The Rudolph Hess mentioned in the story's title was a real-life German politician and deputy head of state during the pre-and early Second World War periods. He flew alone to Scotland with the intention of brokering a peace between his country and Great Britain, but was promptly arrested and held as a prisoner of war for the remainder of the conflict.

[1] Yog-Sothoth L55
НАЗВАНИЕ: Conglomerate ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:13:56 СИМВОЛОВ: 1252 Conglomerate Author Jeffrey Thomas Language English Publisher Necronomicon Press Publication Midnight Shambler November 1996 Conglomerate " is a short Cthulhu Mythos story by American author Jeffrey Thomas . It was first published in the November 1996 edition of the Robert M. Price -edited fanzine Midnight Shambler Synopsis When a crazed vandal kills himself after defacing a company's icon - an enormous, rock-like sphere - head of security Colin James decides to look into the man's motives. What he discovers is that his city was once the site of a titanic battle, one in which Yog-Sothoth was rendered inert by cosmic powers. Furthermore, his company - which he now realises is far more expansive and insidious than he had ever imagined - is responsible for buying the land containing the inactive spheres of the Outer God , linking them together in an attempt to revive the being. The story concludes with James realising that even though there is little he can do against the forces ranged against mankind, he must try before the megacorporation achieves their goal.


--- Copyright status of works by H. P. Lovecraft.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L67
It is unclear whether any of Lovecraft's fictional work meets both criteria. Questions center on who exactly owns or owned the , and whether the post-1928 — including such prominent pieces as At the Mountains of Madness — were renewed as required. Regardless of the legal disagreements surrounding Lovecraft's works, Lovecraft himself was extremely generous with his own works, and actively encouraged others to borrow ideas from his stories, particularly with regard to his Cthulhu Mythos . By "wide citation" he hoped to give his works an "air of verisimilitude", and actively encouraged other writers to reference his creations, such as the Necronomicon Cthulhu and Yog-Sothoth . After his death, many writers have contributed stories and enriched the shared mythology of the Cthulhu Mythos , as well as making numerous references to his work. The Open Cthulhu Mythos project relying on the extreme scholarship of the German Lovecraft Society have prepared a complete and exhaustive list of all Lovecraft works and elements that are beyond question in the public domain as of 2024 and after. Lovecraft had specified that the young R. H.


--- Cosmic Abstract.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L41
Whenever there is a major multiversal event they are either involved as participants or as observers. One Above All = The master of the Multiverse. It is a mysterious supreme being who permits virtually anything to happen in its multiverse, from the birth and creation of new realities to the corruption or destruction of old realities. Living Tribunal = Balance in the multiverse is maintained by the Living Tribunal a being whose power is eclipsed only by the One Above All and whom answers only to the One Above All. Eternity = Similar to how Yog-Sothoth in the Mythos contained within it every universe, likewise the multiversal version of Eternity also contains within it every universe in the multiverse. The Firmaments = Are the beings who embodied the previous multiverses, with the current Eternity being the 8th Cosmos (Multiverse). Each of the universes within the Multiverse has its own pantheon of sorts, consisting of various cosmic abstracts and in some cases a single nigh-omnipotent entity. Each of whose power vastly eclipses that of the most powerful "god" on Earth. Whenever there is a major universal-scale event they are either involved as participants or as observers.


--- Court of Azathoth.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L43
Sometimes it is called "the Final Void". According to some accounts, it awaits behind the last of the Gates Location The Court of Azathoth is located, presumably, in the place beyond the angular space, in which all dimensions come together. Description The Court stands on a plane beyond space and time, serving as the abode for the lobotomized Azathoth , "the foolish Daemon Sultan." There, the almighty Outer God remains dormant by the sounds sung by amorphous flute players. Both Nyarlathotep and Yog-Sothoth are known to visit the Court of Azathoth to review the state he is in after some time. As for its appearance, it can be said that the Court of Azathoth represents the pure essence of chaos: anything strange and surreal that one can imagine has a place in that world that goes beyond logic. Inhabitants The Court of Azathoth is inhabited by amorphous flute players , accompanied by a large group of Outer Gods and Lesser Other Gods .

--- Crypt of Cthulhu (Jack Ryan).txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L51
Consisting of four shorts connected by a wraparound story, it was independently published in October 2018. Both paperback and digital editions were released. Synopsis Dr. Gestalt, a supervising physician at Arkham Asylum , is mystified when four of his most promising patients suddenly slump into a catatonic state for no apparent reason. When the mysterious Dr. Ng arrives with a revolutionary device, the two delve into the patients' dreams, witnessing first hand their recurrent nightmares regarding the evil entities Cthulhu Dagon Yog-Sothoth , and Nyarlathotep At the story's conclusion it is revealed that Dr. Ng is in fact Nyarlathotep himself, and that accessing the minds of the comatose patients was a way to decipher the clues left by Cthulhu on how to awaken him and the other slumbering gods. Gestalt is able to thwart the Outer God's plans, but must sacrifice his own life to do so.

The Cthulhu Eternal Classical Era SRD aims to support a broad spectrum of different types of Lovecraftian game set during this period. Whether you want a gritty and historical tone or something more sword-and-sandals inspired, these rules give you the building blocks to tailor a memorable and evocative Classical Era tale of dread. Whether it's a tense murder mystery amid the complicated political schemings of the Roman forum, or an action packed chase to stop Yog-Sothoth manifesting above the Siege of Troy, these rules have everything you need. It was published by Cthulhu Reborn in 2022. Overview " ... a terrible cosmic narrative derived from ... discourses of the mad self-styled spy who had killed himself. Yuggoth Great Cthulhu Tsathoggua YogSothoth R'lyeh Nyarlathotep Azathoth Cthulhu Eternal is a multi-era, setting agnostic ruleset which aims to support inventive game designers who have original ideas for Lovecraftian roleplaying games or scenarios. It draws upon the long line of D100 games of Cthulhu-themed investigation, offering a beautifully streamlined and elegant set of mechanics to support a diverse range of gaming styles. This version of Cthulhu Eternal is specially designed to support Lovecraftian games set in mid-20th Century, and in particular the shadowy world of the "Cold War" that waxed and waned roughly from the end of World War II to the mid-1990s.

Guide to Arkham Arkham A complete guide to this history, features, and inhabitants of Lovecraft's signature town. Lovecraft's Map of Arkham HPL's hand-drawn map of one of his most famous creations. Guide to Dunwich Dunwich All the points of interest, amenities, local characters, and history of one of Lovecraft's most blighted backwaters.

--- Cthulhu Mythos.txt ---

[1] Kthulhut L83
Rimel Richard F. Searight and others. Lovecraft recognized that each writer had his own story-cycle and that an element from one cycle would not necessarily become part of another simply because a writer used it in one of his stories. For example, although Smith might mention "Kthulhut" ( Cthulhu ) or Iog-Sotôt ( Yog-Sothoth ) in one of his Hyperborean tales , this does not necessarily mean that Cthulhu is part of the Hyperborean Cycle . Whether or not this is the case is a matter of interpretation.

[5] Yog-Sothoth L263
Fungi from Yuggoth features Azathoth and Nyarlathotep alongside Arkham and Innsmouth , while The Whisperer in Darkness mentions them alongside Yuggoth and Cthulhu. " Through the Gates of the Silver Key " is part of the Dream Cycle, yet mentions Yog-Sothoth, Yuggoth, and the Spawn of Cthulhu , etc. However, as with the distinction between the Mythos as a background element versus the Mythos as the focal point of a story, it can be argued that Derleth took the cross-referencing between different story-cycles one step further.

[7] Yog-Sothoth L363
However, as the Mythos has grown and it has become increasingly difficult for any one author to be familiar with all of the elements, the Mythos can been seen as a series of interconnecting cycles of myth that sometimes conflict with one another. The cycles include: the Cthulhu or Xothic Cycle ; the Hastur Cycle ; the Yog-Sothoth Cycle ; the Tsathogguan or Hyperborean Cycle ; the Yig Myth; the Yidhra Cycle ; and the Legend of the Elder Gods . This would reflect the development of real myth, where conflicting versions of the same narrative exist as the legend spreads abroad and is elaborated upon.

[9] Yog-Sothoth L533
Also, Lovecraft explicitly described the Spawn of Cthulhu as land-based creatures, despite looking like "cosmic octopi". Another problem arises when applying the elemental theory to beings that function on a cosmic scale (such as Yog-Sothoth)—some authors have tried to get around this by creating a separate category of aethyr elementals for Azathoth, Shub-Niggurath, Nyarlathotep, and Yog-Sothoth. Finally, Derleth matched the earth beings against the fire beings, and the air beings against the water beings, which is not consistent with the traditional elemental dichotomy (namely, that air opposes earth and fire opposes water).


--- Cthulhu Mythos_ According to August Derleth (Cthulhu Universalis).txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothothery L43
Derleth frequently drew parallels between this rebellion and the fall of Satan. Correspondences between the Great Old Ones and the various elements of Earth, Air, Fire, and Water. The star stones of Mnar, which help to imprison the Great Old Ones and provide protection against their minions. For an overview of Lovecraft's mythos (or "Yog-Sothothery") as he originally developed it, see The Myth Patterns of H. P. Lovecraft . It is not completely clear to me how Derleth came to project the concept of the Elder Gods (1) onto Lovecraft's work. Certainly the two authors had differences of world view and temperament, but the very vagueness and evasiveness of Lovecraft's concepts must have made it easier for Derleth to "fill in the gaps" with his own ideas. Derleth was probably also encouraged by Lovecraft's enthusiastic appreciation for Derleth's early Mythos tales.

Dan expected the birds to stop after an hour and resume just before dawn, but instead they continued all night. Even in daytime, the hills were alive with whippoorwills, and they were ten times as numerous on the slope facing into Harrop’s Pocket. The whippoorwills ceased calling when Amos Whateley set Harrop's house on fire. Deviations of Mythos Canon The distinction between the Great Old Ones and the Outer Gods , while referenced, is largely ignored. Many of the beings traditionally considered Outer Gods, most notably Shub-Niggurath and Nyarlathotep , are referred to as "Great Old Ones." The Night-gaunts are loyal to Nyarlathotep, who in canon was their enemy. Their canonical master, Nodens , is absent and unmentioned in the core game, as are all the Elder Gods The Mi-Go appear to only worship Shub-Niggurath, and are opposed to their other canonical gods Nyarlathotep and Yog-Sothoth The deformities in Wilbur Whateley and the Dunwich Horror are portrayed as a progressive mutation, rather than being present and constant from birth. Ithaqua , rather than merely inspiring the legends of Wendigos, actually has a Wendigo army. Despite their links in canon, Father Dagon Mother Hydra , and the Deep Ones may be played against each other. The Dreamlands do not appear to match Earth's geography. Cultists, which are explicitly Human, appear on Yuggoth without being kidnapped by Mi-Go. This may suggest that map is set in humanity's future. Azathoth does not destroy the universe upon being awakened.

[4] Yog-Sothoth L459
This may suggest that map is set in humanity's future. Azathoth does not destroy the universe upon being awakened. Recruiting neutral monsters allows canonical enemies to serve alongside one another; the Great Race of Yith may fight alongside Flying Polyps , and the Elder Things may fight alongside Shoggoths The Yithians appear in their conical forms where none should be present, such as Modern Earth and Yuggoth. Gobogeg is entirely created by Petersen Games, being "their interpretation" of the thing beyond the mountains at the end of At the Mountains of Madness , a role generally considered to be Yog-Sothoth. The Tcho-Tchos do not appear to worship Zhar and Lloigor The Bhole and the Dhole appear to be separate entities rather than alternate spellings of a single name.

When the bleak truth is revealed, it terrifies us, for it offers no hope of our salvation. Cultists are the gatekeepers to this knowledge. Cthulhu's Dark Cults provides keyhole-glimpses into these secret orders, all irredeemable and hell-bent for humanity's demise. [1] Yog-Sothoth L59
Gesundheit!" Author Len Wein Illustrator Dan Brereton Language English Genre(s) Horror comedy Publisher Bongo Comics Release Date September 2013 "Cthulhu? Gesundheit!" is the third story featured in issue #19 of The Simpsons' Treehouse of Horror series by Bongo Comics. It was written by Len Wein and illustrated by Dan Brereton. Synopsis At Springfield Elementary School, Principal Skinner punishes Bart and his friend Milhouse by forcing them to catalogue all the books in the school's abandoned old library, leading to Bart finding a copy of the Necronomicon . Taking the book back home, Bart explains to Milhouse that it can be used to summon the Great Old Ones to do his bidding and recites the chant " Yog-Sothoth Demonicus Cthulhu ". Meanwhile, Homer was washing his face in the bathroom until one of Cthulhu 's tentacles clogs the sink faucet. At first, Bart uses Cthulhu to get revenge on his enemies, such as killing Skinner and some bullies. Shortly afterwards, Cthulhu goes out of control and starts eating everyone throughout the town. Fearing that it will be the end of the world, Bart and Milhouse go back to the Necronomicon to find a way to stop it.

Lovecraft recognized that each writer had his own story-cycle and that an element from one cycle would not necessarily become part of another simply because a writer used it in one of his stories. For example, although Smith might mention "Kthulhut" (Cthulhu) or Iog-Sotôt (Yog-Sothoth) in one of his Hyperborean tales, this does not necessarily mean that Cthulhu is part of the Hyperborean Cycle. Whether or not this is the case is a matter of interpretation.

[5] Yog-Sothoth L291
Fungi from Yuggoth features Azathoth and Nyarlathotep alongside Arkham and Innsmouth, while The Whisperer in Darkness mentions them alongside Yuggoth and Cthulhu. "Through the Gates of the Silver Key" is part of the Dream Cycle, yet mentions Yog-Sothoth, Yuggoth, and the Spawn of Cthulhu, etc. However, as with the distinction between the Mythos as a background element versus the Mythos as the focal point of a story, it can be argued that Derleth took the cross-referencing between different story-cycles one step further.

[7] Yog-Sothoth L307
However, as the Mythos has grown and it has become increasingly difficult for any one author to be familiar with all of the elements, the Mythos can been seen as a series of interconnecting cycles of myth that sometimes conflict with one another. The cycles include: the Cthulhu or Xothic Cycle; the Hastur Cycle; the Yog-Sothoth Cycle; the Tsathogguan or Hyperborean Cycle; the Yig Myth; the Yidhra Cycle; and the Legend of the Elder Gods. This would reflect the development of real myth, where conflicting versions of the same narrative exist as the legend spreads abroad and is elaborated upon.

[11] Yog-Sothoth L489
The three remaining tales can best be described as dark fantasy. Combined, they cover all of Lovecraft's universe of mind-numbing horror, cosmic beings, outer gods and hidden dangers. [15] Yog-Sothoth L655
In the history of the universe presented in the tome Unaussprechlichen Kulten of Friedrich von Junzt, it is claimed that Cthulhu is the child of Yog-Sothoth and a female denizen of the planet Vhoorl, in the 23rd Nebula.

[16] Yog-Sothoth L655
He also has at least two half-brothers, Hastur and Vulthoom, both sired by Yog-Sothoth on other planets (EXP: "The Horror in the Gallery"), which is consistent with Lovecraft's claim that Yog-Sothoth has fathered numerous children with the native inhabitants of other worlds (HPL: Selected Letters 5.875), as seen in "The Dunwich Horror".

[5] Yog-Sothoth L737
Gordon, Edgar Henquist [RB Demon]: An author of fantasy horror stories that were based on his dreams. His works included Gargoyle, Night-Gaunt, The Principle of Evil, The Soul of Chaos. He was a tall, thin, angular man pale face and deep-set eyes. His language was poetic and profound, and his mannerisms slow and dreamlike. He was descended from a Welsh wizard. He claimed to have seen Azozath, Nyarlathotep, Yog-Sothoth, and Yuggoth in his dreams, prior to reading of their existence in such books as the Necronomicon, Mysteries of the Worm, and the Book of Eibon. Toward the end of his life, his library included occult works such as Cultes des Ghoules and the Daemonolorum. An intelligence called the Dark One instructed Gordon to write his books, and distribute them to "those who know." Someday, Gordon expected to band together with them and unfold secrets of the cosmos.

Cthylla is destined to give birth to Great Cthulhu again after he is destroyed in the distant future.

E. Fassl who has been producing some excellent eye-catching imagery for Chaosium's Call of Cthulhu Fiction line. Interior art comes as normal from the similarly gifted imagination of Dave Carson. [Reviewed by John Goodrich] Just so the reader is aware, I intern for Chaosium, although I don't think that this biases my review. I know a good anthology when I read one. [5] Yog-Sothoth L249
For while our usual anthologists are very dedicated to the Mythos, quite often they do not have many contacts in the greater world of horror fiction. Mr. Rainey, who edited Deathrealm for ten years, seems able to call upon a broader base of writers. The linking thread of the anthology is the Mythos set to music. From Erich Zann's daemonic viol to the hard rocking sound of Dew, and even a touch of the Great White Way, Song of Cthulhu offers us the musical world with Yog-Sothoth as our tour guide. I'd like to hold a few of these stories up to aspiring Mythos authors as good examples of how to write a good Mythos story. Far too often, eager young boys, we Mythos authors go straight for the good stuff -- a hint of something inhuman on the first page or a Lovecraftian name dropped. But this lack of confidence is exactly the opposite of what made Lovecraft's fiction so effective at evoking mood.

[8] Yog-Sothoth L303
E. A. Lustig's "The Enchanting of Lila Woods" is another example of a tale that's well-told but ultimately formulaic. I did like the characterization of Maeve McKiernan (name Irish enough for you?) and the other people at Arkham House -- it's not often you see servants of the Great Old Ones developed into real sympathetic characters, so this was a nice change. "Yog-Sothoth, Superstar" is a joky story about the progress of the musical Lovecraft in Love and its disastrous consequences on cast members, critics, and eventually most of the population of Manhattan. It's more ambitious formally than many Mythos tales, incorporating excerpts from songbooks, letter, memos, answering machine messages, et. al. Overall I'd say this is a good but not great anthology. Several of the tales have formulaic plots, not always overcome by prose style and characterization. This might be one to check out at the library or used bookstores. P. Lovecraft have been an influence on his own. At age 11 or 12, he first discovered Lovecraft through the short story " The Colour Out of Space "; he later sought out more of his fiction, as it had had such a profound effect on him. He has also claimed that when writing the screenplay for Alien , he had intended for there to be a direct connection between the Xenomorphs and the Outer God Yog-Sothoth ; this was removed from the final draft. His claim is perhaps recognised in the finale of the prequel movie Alien: Covenant , when the antagonist removes human embryos from storage and replaces them with Xenomorph embryos, to the tune of Wagner's "Das Rheingold" (popularly known in English as "Entry Of the Gods Into Valhalla").

[1] Yog-Sothoth L89
P. Lovecraft 's novella At the Mountains of Madness . Written by Christopher Michael, the series blends elements of World War II espionage with themes and entities drawn from the Cthulhu Mythos The series presents Danforth as an intelligence operative whose prior exposure to incomprehensible cosmic forces during the Antarctic expedition has left him psychologically scarred and uniquely vulnerable to further encounters with forbidden knowledge. Premise Set during the Second World War, the series follows Danforth as he becomes involved in covert intelligence operations intersecting with occult phenomena. Drawing upon historical events and locations, the narrative situates Mythos elements beneath real-world wartime espionage, portraying cosmic horror Throughout the series, Danforth struggles with trauma, nihilism, and the lingering effects of his earlier encounter with the alien city in Antarctica Mythos Connections Danforth: Eldritch Tales of WWII incorporates numerous established elements of the Cthulhu Mythos , including references to the Necronomicon Nyarlathotep Yog-Sothoth Ghatanothoa , and many others. These entities and concepts are presented in a manner consistent with Lovecraftian themes of cosmic indifference and the limits of human understanding. The series is a derivative literary work inspired by the writings of H. P. Lovecraft and later Mythos authors. It is not part of Lovecraft’s original canon.

[1] Тот L49
Слишком самонадеянно кичились они своим мастерством охоты на диких биопотов, хотя большая часть их успеха достигалась применением полуприрученных курешей, одновременно в качестве охотничьих собак и верховых животных. Это отвратительное ископаемое древних времен, давно вымершее в других областях Сказочной Страны, имело, в сущности, конское тело, на которое садились верхом наиболее отважные вожди, длинную узкую собачью морду, позволяющую брать след на больших расстояниях, и огромные когти, которые вместе с пастью, полной крупных неровных клыков, делали много больше вреда на охоте, чем их несовершенные копья. Судя по всему, людей Югироута не беспокоил тот факт, что норовистые животные забирают себе львиную долю как в охотниках, так и в добыче, ибо если охота оказывалась успешной, оставалось довольно много, чтобы поделить трофеи, а если нет, павшие участники утоляли голод тех, кто числился в живых. Даже приручение животных было за пределами способностей югироутивян. Их обучали и воспитывали другие, более внушительные и зловещие существа. Однако их представление о времени было столь смутным, что они не могли сказать, десять ли, десять тысяч ли веков прошло с того дня, когда Существо в Желтой Маске пришло и научило их изготавливать копья, есть мясо и ездить верхом на курешах. А когда их спрашивали, что Существо потребовало взамен, они только зловеще ухмылялись и делали каменные лица.

--- Dictionary of Celtic Myth and Legend (Green, Miranda J.) (z-library.sk, 1lib.sk, z-lib.sk).txt ---

[1] The Key L15231
This symbolism of the afterlife may also be represented on images where Epona carries a large KEY; this occurs, for instance, at Gannat (Allier) and Grand (Vosges). The motif could represent the key to the stable, but at a deeper level, it could reflect the ability of the goddess to unlock the gates of heaven and the happy Otherworld. On other images, as at Mussig- Vicenz near Strasbourg, Epona holds a mappa or napkin which, we are told by Suetonius (Nero 22), was used to start off horse races. Again, at a more profound level of meaning, the mappa may reflect Epona’s presiding over the beginning of man’s journey through life.

[6] The Key L22357
At Winchester (Hants) a wooden image of a goddess wearing a cloak and tore bears a mappa (napkin) and a large key. The mappa was regularly used by the Romans to signal the start of horse races; Webster has suggested that, in a symbolic context, the mappa may reflect the beginning of life. If this is so then the key may symbolize the end of earthly existence and the journey through the entrance to the underworld. A sculpture at Naix (Meuse) shows a Mother-goddess with two younger attendants, one of whom has a vessel and key. The pot may be concerned with renewal (see CAULDRON), and the key may again refer to the gates of heaven.

The theme of the 'calumniated wife’ comes in when Rhiannon’s baby son, PRYDERI, born after many years of waiting for an heir, was spirited away on the eve of 1 May (the Feast of Beltene), and she was falsely accused of murdering him by the women on watch. Old Whateley The Dunwich Horror is a fictional entity created by H. P. Lovecraft for his eponymous short story Background The Dunwich Horror is the inhuman child of Lavinia Whateley and Yog-Sothoth , who was conceived to free the Great Old Ones so that they may reclaim the Earth . Its existence was kept secret by its grandfather, mother and eventually its twin brother, Wilbur Whateley . It fed on cattle growing up, draining them of blood before devouring them completely. The intense stench of the abomination kept away most passersby. On September 9, 1928, the creature broke free from the Whateley farmhouse, littering the hillside with wooden planks soaked with an odd viscous substance. Barrel-sized tracks were found leading to a meadow where over half a herd of cows were drained of blood.

--- Elder Gods and Great Old Ones.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L19
НАЗВАНИЕ: Elder Gods and Great Old Ones ИСТОЧНИК: God Terminology in Derleth's Mythos Stories As scholars first pointed out in the 1970s ( fn1 ), August Derleth's version of the Mythos differs significantly from that of H. P. Lovecraft by introducing a set of benign gods ( fn2 ) who are responsible for having imprisoned the various Lovecraftian gods (such as Azathoth Yog-Sothoth Cthulhu , and so on). August Derleth's view of the two groups of gods remained fairly consistent throughout his writings. However, his terminology for referring to these groups varied significantly over his career, most especially in his early stories. In the majority of Derleth's best-known Mythos stories, the beneficent deities are referred to as the Elder Gods, and the malign deities are referred to primarily as the Great Old Ones or the Ancient Ones. However, in some stories, other terms are used, or the meanings of the usual terms are even reversed.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L469
Or he might have changed his views about how to write this type of story effectively. Footnotes fn1 . Tierney, Richard L. , "The Derleth Mythos"(1972) and Mosig, Dirk, "H. P. Lovecraft: Myth-Maker" (1976), reprinted in S. T. Joshi (ed.) , Dissecting Cthulhu: Essays on the Cthulhu Mythos . Lakeland, FL: Miskatonic River Press, 2011. Tierney's essay is also available in Schweitzer, Darrell (ed.) , Discovering H. P. Lovecraft . Wildside Press. Kindle Edition. fn2 . By "deities" or "gods" I am referring to the more powerful entities in the Mythos ( Yog-Sothoth Azathoth Nyarlathotep , etc.) , that are commonly worshipped by less powerful species such as the Deep Ones Outer Ones , and the spawn of Cthulhu . I am aware that some scholars believe these entities should not be referred to as "gods," at least not in Lovecraft's own work. fn3 . Haefele, John D. A Look Behind the Derleth Mythos: Origins of the "Cthulhu Mythos" . The Cimmerian Press: 2014. Return to CthulhuFiles.

( HPL Selected Letters of H. P. Lovecraft 3.439) The Hay Necronomicon also represented the Elder Sign as a gesture which consisted of joining the tips of one's thumb and little fingers. It also described the sign of Voor, of Kisk and of Koth. An item called the Elder Sign appears in the video game Ogre Battle 64 for the Nintendo 64. It can only be equipped by magic using classes.
