--- The Creeper in the Crypt.txt ---

[1] The Key L81
Sewell Street, the location of Tarleton's party. Pringle Street, the address of the Chambers house. Old Town Street, where Cyrus Hook's mansion was burned down. The Chambers House The story's primary location is the Chambers house, also know as the Dark house, known as "the moldering house with the iron door in the cellar." Built on Pringle Street, it was originally owned by the colonial wizard Ezekiel Chambers, and then by the smuggler/graverobber Jonathan Dark. Dark was accused as using the door "as a passageway for bringing his stolen cadavers back to dispose of," but the door was not opened after his arrest; he made the "astounding and hideous claim that the key which locked it was on the other side. " Dark also claimed that the tenants of the graveyard "would come to visit the house from below when a wizard invoked it with the proper spells and sacrifice." The Graveyard on the Hill Next to the Chambers house is "the old graveyard on the hill"; this corresponds to the "Wooded Graveyard" on "Hangman's Hill" that appears on Lovecraft's map. Dark claimed that below the graveyard there were "tunnels and burrows and secret vaults used in witch-days for unhallowed rites", and that these vaults had "tenants".

During her quest to collect the other keys, Page travelled across several alternate realities and took the role of a different alter ego in each one. She first appeared as a barbarian known as "Bettie the Page" in Hyperborea , where she gained superior strength and swordsmanship to defeat Count Vizier, an evil sorcerer who was under the influence of Nyarlathotep . In the next reality, she becomes a vampire-lady from the planet Vampiron. When the chief inquisitor Benway tried to commit genocide against their race, the Ruling Council of Vampiron attempted to save their world by summoning Yog-Sothoth. In another reality, she becomes a princess of Xenon and encounters the genocidal Benway again, who ends up summoning Azathoth in order to destroy the city of the Puru. Finally, she takes the form of a tiny fairy who allies herself with a mermaid version of her best friend Melyssa and a group of pirates to fight off Cthulhu . With their help, she successfully used the five keys to banish the Great Old Ones, saving the entire multiverse from destruction and transporting Page back to her home world.

[1] Yog-Sothoth L87
What Edgar Gordon did for me in the next three years can never adequately be told. His able assistance, friendly criticism and kind encouragement finally succeeded in making a writer of sorts out of me. Gordon confides to the narrator that his stories--with titles like The Soul of Chaos and The Principle of Evil --all come from his dreams. In sleep, he has repeatedly visited the "[m]ountains of black stalagmites; peaks and cones amidst crater valleys of dead suns; [and] stone cities in the stars" that reoccur in his dreams. He admits that his stories echo "descriptive passages in such books as the Necronomicon , the Mysteries of the Worm , and the Book of Eibon ," but insists that he had prior knowledge of Azozath [sic] and Yuggoth before learning that they appeared in such books, and could describe Nyarlathotep and Yog-Sothoth from "actual dream contact with these allegorical entities." The narrator becomes concerned when Gordon becomes obsessed with an entity known as "the Dark One ", the Demon Messenger, who has chosen Gordon "to be the Messiah; the messenger of His word." (As any fan of the Cthulhu Mythos would, the narrator wonders if this character is "remotely connected with the Nyarlathotep fable.") The Dark One appears to Gordon as "looking like Asmodeus--black all over, and furry, with green eyes, hog snout, and the claws and fangs of some wild beast."

--- The Dream-Quest of Vellitt Boe.txt ---

[1] The Gate L63
When her best student, Clarie Jurat, runs off with a man from the waking world, Boe must relearn her travelling ways and bring her back--first to prevent Clarie's trustee father from shutting down the school, and later, when it turns out that Clarie's maternal grandfather is a sleeping god, to keep him from destroying Ulthar and the plains of the River Skai. Vellitt journeys to Hatheg-Kla, in hopes of exiting through the Gate of Deeper Slumber; to Ilek-Vad , in hopes of obtaining the Silver Key ; and through the Underworld to Sarkomand , where the ghouls have a secret staircase to the waking world; and to the fabled lands of Wisconsin and Montana, where people are "random and meaningful and beautiful."


--- The Druid of Castle Rock.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L69
It is the fourth story in Book 2 of his Nyarlathotep Cycle Synopsis Field agent Malcolm Mayweather is assigned on bodyguard duty to Isla Urquhart, a researcher in the British counterpart to the Department of Extraordinary Phenomena . Part of his task is to assist the researcher in testing out new technology which will help identify the taint of The Other. Their testing takes the two from the highlands of Scotland to its capital Edinburgh, where they locate a cult to Yog-Sothoth hiding in plain sight. Although Mayweather is captured by the cultists, Urquhart calls in backup and the worshippers are brought to account. Characters Malcolm Mayweather , a former firefighter, now a rookie field agent in the Department of Extraordinary Phenomena. Isla Urquhart , a brilliant technical researcher for the British equivalent to the department. Harjit Singh , director of the department. "The Druid of Castle Rock" was published in the collection The Other: Encounters with the Cthulhu Mythos Book 2 in 2020.

--- The Dunwich Horror.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L279

( EXP The Dunwich Horror and Others The tracks of Wilbur's brother recall those seen in Algernon Blackwood 's " The Wendigo ", one of Lovecraft's favorite horror stories. Plot summary In the isolated, desolate, decrepit village of Dunwich, Wilbur Whateley is the hideous son of Lavinia Whateley , a deformed and unstable albino mother, and an unknown father (alluded to in passing by mad Old Whateley , as " Yog-Sothoth "). Strange events surround his birth and precocious development. Wilbur matures at an abnormal rate, reaching manhood within a decade. Locals shun him and his family, and animals fear and despise him (due to his odor). All the while, his sorcerer grandfather indoctrinates him into certain dark rituals and the study of witchcraft .

[2] Yog-Sothoth L287
Wilbur matures at an abnormal rate, reaching manhood within a decade. Locals shun him and his family, and animals fear and despise him (due to his odor). All the while, his sorcerer grandfather indoctrinates him into certain dark rituals and the study of witchcraft . Various locals grow suspicious after Old Whateley buys more and more cattle, yet the number of his herd never increases, and the cattle in his field become mysteriously afflicted with severe open wounds. Wilbur and his grandfather have sequestered an unseen presence at their farmhouse; this being is connected somehow to Yog-Sothoth. Year by year, this unseen entity grows to monstrous proportions, requiring the two men to make frequent modifications to their residence. People begin to notice a trend of cattle mysteriously disappearing. Wilbur's grandfather dies. His mother disappears soon afterwards. The colossal entity eventually occupies the whole interior of the farmhouse. Wilbur ventures to Miskatonic University in Arkham to procure their copy of the Necronomicon — Miskatonic's library is one of only a handful in the world to stock an original.

[3] Yog-Sothoth L415
She is described as a somewhat deformed, unattractive albino woman... a lone creature given to wandering amidst thunderstorms in the hills and trying to read the great odorous books which her father had inherited through two centuries of Whateleys.... She had never been to school, but was filled with disjointed scraps of ancient lore that Old Whateley had taught her.... Isolated among strange influences, Lavinia was fond of wild and grandiose day-dreams and singular occupations. Elsewhere, she is called "slatternly [and] crinkly-haired". In 1913, she gave birth to Wilbur Whateley by an unknown father, later revealed to be Yog-Sothoth . Presumably, she is either forced or coerced into mating with Yog-Sothoth by her father, Old Whateley. On Halloween night in 1926, she disappeared under mysterious circumstances, most likely killed or sacrificed by her son, whom the villagers claimed had an immense dislike of Lavinia. --- The Electric Executioner.txt ---

[2] Yog-Sototl L109
Realizing his bluff has run its course, the narrator moves to another. This time, he appeals to the stranger's cultist side, and pretends to be the human messenger or incarnation of an Aztec god. Trembling at the names Huitzilopotchli, Tloquenahuaque, and Ipalnemoan (Ipalnemohuani), the stranger falls to his knees, and ecstatically replies with the names Mictlanteuctli, Tonatiuh-Metztli, but also the name " Cthulhutl ." The narrator is in luck: they recognize the name "Cthulhutl" from whispers among the Mexican miners, and so responds with the names of even more gods and mythical figures: " Ya-R'lyeh , Niguratl-Yig (a combination of Yig and presumably Shub-Niggurath ), and finally " Yog-Sototl ." The stranger is so overcome by this display that their frantic worshipping pulls the battery off the seat, and it strikes the ground, causing the mask to activate and kill the stranger. This horrible death is so shocking to witness that the narrator faints. Forty years later, the narrator still does not know what truly happened in the train car: a stress dream, astral projection, or some other explanation. He wonders if Feldon was truly in the car, or if he, the narrator, was somehow in the cave in Mexico?

B. Yeats, James Joyce, and Ezra Pound, among others. The book is organized as a series of sketches about an imaginary pantheon; the concept was a key influence on H. P. --- The Larkhill Barrow.txt ---

[1] The Gate L51
Synopsis Famous occultist Thomas Carnacki is summoned to assist a military man with a problem his unit have been having at their training facility: every time they test a new machine gun atop a rise in the ground, it results in the shooter going insane (an effect which dissipates after a short time) and the whole camp suffering from dreadful dreams of drums - and something far more sinister - in the dark (which does not). Carnacki's investigations revealed that the rise is in fact an ancient barrow designed as a kind of sonic prison for an ancient and malevolent entity, and the rhythmic drum of the machine gun has partially opened the gate. Luckily for everyone, Carnacki is able to reproduce the effects of the prison through the use of phonograph recordings and many mystical charms, and even manages to re-incarcerate the entity on one of his phonograph cylinders, a fact he keeps hidden from everyone involved. Characters Thomas Carnacki , a renowned occult detective. Private Jimmy Carruthers , a brave 18 year old soldier who assists Carnacki in his efforts. [1] The Gate L103
Then, then discover why, as they find both Mad Dan and his wife petrified inside, Dan tied to a chair with a leather whip, and Rose strangely smug in her final moments. The pair find Dan's diary on the table, which tells the story in great detail. Dan is the decedent of a certain Nicolas Van Kauran , a wizard once burned at the stake, though his copy of the Book of Eibon survived, and was passed down through the generations. Dan continues to perform ancient rites into the present, including sacrificing to Shubb-Niggurath , and complaining that the villagers "always prevent my doing the Great Rite that would open the gate." Rose also does not participate in his ceremonies, much to his complaints, and when Wheeler arrives and Dan notices their flirting, he contrives a horrible revenge. After several months of study (where Dan discards ideas like, "the emanation of with ," or "The Green Decay") Morris finds a weapon with a poetic flourish: a potion to induce petrification, once used for murder by another ancestor. Admitting it has more to do with science than magic, he constructs a secret laboratory in the cave, testing his formulas on passing animals.

--- The Mannikin.txt ---

[1] The Opener of the Way L139
The Algonquin-sounding name of the Indians whose legends Maglore inquires into--the Pasquantog--suggests a New England setting. After its initial Weird Tales appearance, "The Mannikin" was frequently reprinted. It appeared in Sleep No More: Twenty Masterpieces of Horror for the Connoisseur , a 1944 anthology edited by August Derleth , as well as The Seventh Fontana Book of Great Horror Stories (1972) and The Sixth Mayflower Book of Black Magic Stories (1977). It's often included in collections of Bloch's short stories, including The Opener of the Way Arkham House , 1945); Yours Truly, Jack the Ripper (Belmont, 1962); The House of the Hatchet and Other Tales of Horror (Tandem, 1965); Mysteries of the Worm (Zebra, 1981; Chaosium , 1993); and The Early Fears Fedogan & Bremer , 1994).

Убежали, когда подъехал мой грузовик. Но они могут вернуться, когда поймут, что я один. Пойдемте. Мы увезем вас отсюда. Старик не ответил. Лео помог ему подняться и, полунеся, довел до ожидавшего пикапа. Он усадил его в кабину, затем забрался с другой стороны за руль.

--- The Old Gods Awaken.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L67
When a new star appears in the heavens where no star was before, astronomers class it as a supernova and study it with avid interest, but its novelty is soon taken for granted by the general public. Unknown to all, it is the fulfillment of an ancient prophecy in the Necronomicon . When the stars come right, the Old Gods shall rise again from their places of waiting beneath the sea, under the ground, and between the dimensions of space. The blind idiot, Azathoth , has piped a cosmic song on his cracked flute, and once more the gates of Yog-Sothoth yawn wide to admit nightmares from forgotten ages into our modern world.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L143
H. P. Lovecraft envisioned many terrifying Elder Gods Old Ones and Deep Ones as part of his Cthulhu Mythos. Donald Tyson has written a series of horrific stories set in that world especially for this volume, in which eleven of these primordial deities from beyond the stars we know are represented—and in which the threats they pose to the continuing existence of humanity are made clear. Or, in some cases, subverted. But take heed of these warnings! A new, menacing red star approaches in the not-so-heavenly heavens. --- The Opener of the Way (story).txt ---

[1] The Opener of the Way L1
НАЗВАНИЕ: The Opener of the Way (story) ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:32:22 СИМВОЛОВ: 2665 The Opener of the Way Author Robert Bloch Language English Genre(s) Cthulhu Mythos Publication Weird Tales Publication date October 1936 WT "The Opener of the Way" is a short story by Robert Bloch that appeared in the October 1936 issue of Weird Tales . It served as the title story of Bloch's first Arkham House collection, The Opener of the Way (1945). It is included in the third edition of his collection of Mythos fiction, Mysteries of the Worm Chaosium , 2009). Synopsis An embittered archeologist, Sir Ronald Barton, along with his son and assistant Peter Barton, finds a hidden tomb in Egypt . He is guided by a pilfered parchment written in Chaldean, which describes how to evade the tomb's elaborate curse.

[2] The Opener of the Way L83
Described as "a tall, thin man with a face as wrinkled as the papyrus parchment he clutched.... His white hair, sunken eyes and yellowed skin gave him the aspect of an old man." He had "dabbled in sorcery, a bit." Peter Barton: A "younger replica" of his father, though his "voice was not nearly as loud or as firm". He "really loved his father," but is "more than a little afraid of Sir Ronald". Behind the Mythos "The Opener of the Way" was not included in the first two editions of Mysteries of the Worm , reflecting its subtle connection to the Cthulhu Mythos. Referring to Sir Ronald's parchment and the Egyptian priest who wrote it, the story states: The enchanter who had written it alluded to gods far older than those he worshipped. There was mention of the 'Demon Messenger' and the 'Black Temple', coupled with the secret myth and legend-cycles of pre-Adamite days. While in the parchment, the "names of these accursed ones were set forth", they are not specified in the story.

[3] The Opener of the Way L95
There was mention of the 'Demon Messenger' and the 'Black Temple', coupled with the secret myth and legend-cycles of pre-Adamite days. While in the parchment, the "names of these accursed ones were set forth", they are not specified in the story. The "Demon Messenger", however, is cited as a epithet of Nyarlathotep in Bloch's story " The Faceless God ". (In "The Opener of the Way", Peter Barton recalls the "terrible rumors concerning the end of that unsavory adventurer, Doctor Carnoti"; "Carnoti" was the name of the protagonist in early versions of "The Faceless God", later changed to "Stugatche".) There is one more explicit Mythos tie-in in the story, when Sir Ronald declares, "Now I know what Prinn must have meant in his chapter on the Saracenic rituals ; the part where he spoke of the 'symbols on the gate'."

[4] The Gate L105

--- The Overseer (Kingdom Rush series).txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L57
Before coming to this galaxy, the Overseer nearly destroyed another world inhabited by powerful heroes. However, these heroes united and managed to defeat it. Kingdom Rush: Alliance The events of Legends of Kingdom Rush reveal that the malevolent Overseer had already begun infiltrating the realm of Linerea. A group of people, blinded by his influence, formed the Unblinded Cult. Their goal was to create an opening for the Overseer into their world, allowing him to consume it as he had countless others before. Trivia The Overseer bears a strong resemblance to Cyäegha , or arguably, Yog-Sothoth himself. Images of the tentacles, a Lovecraftian trademark, are also recurring throughout the series. The minions Cult Abomination and Taskmaster Abomination serving the Overseer are clearly inspired by the iconic Cthulhu himself.

[2] The Key L81
Erimem's father, Pharaoh Amenhotep II, came into possession of certain scrolls which described creatures older and more fearsome than the gods themselves. Erimem recalls seeing these scrolls as a child, and how the pictures gave her nightmares. She witnesses the Great Old Ones laying waste to the biosphere of entire planets, which leaves her horrified, but the vision argues that these massacres were a positive thing, as they gave life on these worlds a second chance to evolve again. When informed that she is the key to releasing these creatures, Erimem counters that she can't do so if she's dead. As a result, she sees her own body preserved in the ice, still capable of being revived. Part Three At the hotel, the Doctor and Peri investigate the ground that the cloud monster passed over, finding the marks of claws suggestive of a strange reptilian creature. The Doctor concludes that the monster is made from organic material, psychically animated and given life to by a far more powerful being. General Bruce agrees to organise an expedition to the mountain.

[1] The Opener of the Way L47
НАЗВАНИЕ: The Shambler from the Stars ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:32:57 СИМВОЛОВ: 4149 The Shambler from the Stars Author Robert Bloch Country United States Language English Genre(s) Lovecraftian Horror Mystery WT The Shambler from the Stars " is a horror short story by American writer Robert Bloch , first published in the September 1935 issue of Weird Tales . It is the first story of the Robert Blake Cycle It was later included as part of his first published book, The Opener of the Way (1945), and his 1994 collection The Early Fears . A Cthulhu Mythos tale, it introduced the forbidden tome De Vermis Mysteriis Mysteries of the Worm ), although it had been earlier mentioned in the short story " The Secret in the Tomb ". Later on in 1935, Lovecraft wrote the short story " The Haunter of the Dark " as a sequel and dedicated it to Bloch.

--- The Silver Key.txt ---

[1] The Key L95
Hoffmann Price The story and its sequel both feature Lovecraft's recurring character of Randolph Carter as the protagonist. Synopsis silver key in his attic, inscribed with mysterious arabesque symbols, which he finds and takes with him on a visit to his boyhood home in the backwoods of northeastern Massachusetts (the setting for many of Lovecraft's stories), where he enters a mysterious cave that he used to play in. The key somehow enables him to return to his childhood as a ten-year-old boy, and his adult self disappears from his normal time. The story then relates how Randolph's relatives had noted, beginning at the age of ten, that he had somehow gained the ability to glimpse events in his future. The narrator of the story then states that he expects to meet Randolph soon, in one of his own dreams, "in a certain dream-city we both used to haunt", reigning there as a new king, where the narrator may look at Randolph's key, whose symbols he hopes will tell him the mysteries of the cosmos.

Она сопротивлялась, но так легко было бы принять предложенное, низвергнуть Зикакиса и поставить себя на его место.

--- The Whippoorwills in the Hills.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L89
At night, Dan is kept awake by the incessant callings of a flock of whippoorwills , which are noticeably larger and noisier than usual. According to local folklore, whippoorwills can capture the soul of a person who's dying, so the birds' activity is taken as a bad omen. Back in the Harrop house, Dan decides to read some of the books to get to the bottom of the mystery. He finds some marked passages, one of which cautions the reader about summoning Yog-Sothoth and other entities, who demand blood when summoned, and will feed on the summoner themself if the latter has no other sacrifice to offer. That night, Dan manages to fall asleep, despite the cacophony of the whippoorwills, but wakes up in the middle of the night by a different sound: that of a thunderous, pulsating chant in an unknown language which includes the name Yog-Sothoth. The whippoorwills seem to call rhythmically, as if responding to the chant. Although Dan is unable to identify the source of the chant, he feels that it is extremely close: inside the house, or even inside his room.

That night, Dan manages to fall asleep, despite the cacophony of the whippoorwills, but wakes up in the middle of the night by a different sound: that of a thunderous, pulsating chant in an unknown language which includes the name Yog-Sothoth. The whippoorwills seem to call rhythmically, as if responding to the chant. Although Dan is unable to identify the source of the chant, he feels that it is extremely close: inside the house, or even inside his room. He remains paralysed with fear until the strange ritual ends with the sound of earth-shaking footsteps moving away, and the fluttering of the whippoorwills taking off. In the morning, Dan is still shaken by his experience.

[3] Yog-Sothoth L95

[4] Yog-Sothoth L115

In the morning, he wakes up feeling as tired as if he had spent the night labouring, and learns that seven more cows have been found dead and bloodless. The following night, Dan has the same dream, this time aware of being one of the servitors of Yog-Sothoth itself, the mightiest of all the Ancient Ones. Even while dreaming, he can still hear the alien chant and the whippoorwills. Dan ends the narrative by revealing what others have told him: that it was Dan himself who was chanting all along, and that he was found drinking the blood of a woman whose throat he had torn apart, surrounded by the flock of restless whippoorwills. In his final rant, Dan alternates between reaffirming his loyalty to Yog-Sothoth and proclaiming his innocence, blaming the woman's death on the whippoorwills.

--- The White People.txt ---

[1] The Lurker at the Threshold L111
I may write something about all these things but not the way to do them, for peculiar reasons. And I must not say who the Nymphs are, or the Dôls, or Jeelo, or what voolas mean. This passage is the source for the Aklo language mentioned by H. P. Lovecraft in " The Dunwich Horror The Haunter of the Dark ", and " The Diary of Alonzo Typer ". Aklo is also mentioned in August Derleth The Lurker at the Threshold , which references the Chian language and the Mao Games as well. Later, the girl mentions "the kingdom of Voor, where the light goes when it is put out, and the water goes when the sun takes it away." She uses the word "voor" or "voorish" a few ways, in contexts that seem to mean "darkness", e. g. : I saw the terrible voor again on everything, for though the sky was brighter, the ring of wild hills all around was still dark, and the hanging woods looked dark and dreadful, and the strange rocks were as grey as ever....

Он мог часами пялиться на них, пытаясь проследить ту единственную нить, что приведет его к скрытому образу, который он искал. Но такие абстракции были так же ограничены в своих рамках, как и картины. Рано или поздно ему пришлось бы расширить поле исследований, чтобы охватить сам видимый мир. Однако это представляло свои проблемы. Он достаточно читал о психологии восприятия, чтобы знать: то, что человек видит, во многом определяется тем, что он ожидает увидеть. Его собственные ожидания были сформированы всей жизнью, в течение которой он видел тот же мир, что и другие. Это могло лишь помешать тому восприятию, которого он теперь добивался. Следовательно, он должен был научиться отделять значение от зрелища. Он должен был научиться разбивать окружающий мир на абстракцию цвета и текстуры, не обращая внимания на предметы и формы. Теоретически это было легче, чем на практике. И все же бывали моменты, пусть и краткие, когда он чувствовал, что действительно может растворить мир вокруг себя и свести его к абстрактному узору, столь же бессмысленному на вид, как любой стереограмматический отпечаток.

Том не мог отпустить его без расспросов. Он побежал к нему, крича, чтобы тот подождал. Старик не остановился и не обернулся. Но, должно быть, он все же услышал Тома, потому что внезапно ускорил шаг. Но в любом случае он не смог бы уйти намного дальше, поскольку у переулка не было другого выхода, кроме того, через который они вошли.

Сбросив стопку книг, она села на трон колдуна, положила клинок себе на колени. Она скрестила ноги и позволила одной босой, красивой ступне болтаться впереди. — Инмор'лех... — произнесла она, раскатывая слово языком. Она произнесла тайное имя смело и без страха. — Тот город, — выдохнул колдун, — запретный... — Он пытался подняться на ноги. Мера закрыла глаза. Она не смела открыть ни одному капитану, которого нанимала, своего тайного пункта назначения, ибо сказание о Каксе иссушало мужество всех, кто разворачивал паруса или греб веслами в такт барабанам. О, если бы я только не был добычей той особой алчности, что просыпается при возможности незаработанного богатства, той страсти игрока, извращенного зуда рискнуть всем. В тот вечер мы не дали обещания, но к утру решили присоединиться к Ульмхаасу и его планам. Вернее, решил я, а Тохран был готов поддержать меня, хотя и не без оговорок. Маги, ученые и им подобные заставляли его медлить, особенно после уверений его родителей, что волшебники Гипербореи обладают истинным тайным знанием и силой и не забавляются шарлатанским кривлянием. О плавании в Ур-Эйрибос я скажу немного; само путешествие было по большей части спокойным и столь же утомительным, как и любое другое — не заблуждайтесь, скука в море предпочтительнее.

[5] Той L209
Большой сундук остался на пляже: люди, которым поручили его тащить, были слишком изранены, чтобы погрузить его на борт. Жизнь важнее золота, пусть оно там и лежит. Вернувшись на посудину капитана, мы подсчитали потери. Одному человеку раздробило ногу, и ее пришлось отнять — я после выплачивал ему пенсию. У других были раны, но такие, что со временем зажили благодаря врачеванию Ульмхааса. Выслушав наш рассказ, капитан настоял на том, чтобы сняться с якоря и уходить. Ульмхаас был в ярости, так как в той подземной библиотеке оставалось еще много материалов, которые он намеревался забрать. Капитан посмотрел на него ошеломленно. — Разве вы еще не знаете? Обернитесь, гипербореец, — и видите черный дым! Ваша сокровищница тайн горит! Так оно и было. Один из матросов с виноватым видом вспомнил, что оставил свой факел в склепе, погашенным, но, возможно, не до конца потухшим. Тохран допустил, что и он мог сделать то же самое, хотя, быть может, щадил чувства моряка. Старый пергамент и папирус горят как трут; Ульмхаас рухнул на колени, причитая.

[7] Тот L227
Некоторые размахивали кинжалами или трезубцами, большинство полагалось на свои когтистые руки. Они походили на колдуна-жреца, но были коренастее; на тех шеях, что у них были, пульсировали жабры. Завязался ужасный бой, мы с Токраном были в авангарде, рубя мечами. В те дни я неплохо владел оружием, но Тохран сражался куда более впечатляюще, чем можно было поверить. Я знал его как мечника заслуженной славы, но в тот день он, казалось, стал единым целым со своим клинком, с быстротой и мрачной яростью выцеливая и поражая изрядное число вооруженных отвратительных пришельцев. Было похоже, что он рожден и воспитан для этого, — и, подозреваю, так оно и было. Ульмхаас поднялся с нижней палубы, неся охапку странных золотых украшений. Он сунул их ошеломленному захватчику и залопотал что-то на неведомом языке, извлекая шар и угрожающе держа его. Тварь отпрянула, шипя, испустила странный завывающий крик и прыгнула за борт со своей ношей.

[1] Той L7
Меня зовут Александр Флетчер, и для стороннего взгляда я до самого недавнего времени вёл тихое, учёное существование, посвящённое исследованиям и знанию, существование, которое лишь продолжало увлечённость архаичным и древним, занимавшую меня с самых ранних лет, когда во время многих мальчишеских прогулок по сельской местности, окружавшей место моего рождения в Дорсете, я натыкался то на кремнёвый наконечник стрелы, то на загадочный костяной инструмент, оставленный доисторическими обитателями той земли, и обнаруживал, что моё воображение воспламенено мыслями о минувших глубинах истории, сокрытом знании и первобытной легенде. [4] The Key L107
My lot was made bearable only by the goal to which my work would lead, and surely a lifelong dedication to scholastic discipline did much to mitigate the spiritual degradation inescapably concomitant with the magical practices I undertook after a lengthy study of the manuscript I had borne away from that isolated manor house. That my praxis resulted in real, perceptible, and physical effects I could not deny, and it was with a mixture of elation and disgust that I regarded the results of my first operations: elation because I knew that I had now come into possession of the key that would unlock the means to my revenge, disgust because I had now become a member of a corrupt brotherhood of cultic ignorance, one that linked with repugnant intimacy the jungle savage and the educated practitioner, and united the degenerate slum dweller with the elegant sophisticate in an incestuous amalgam of deviant methodology. Nor did I refrain from seizing every available opportunity to add to my knowledge and my practice, for the manuscript, while quite usable in its own fashion, contained only the most basic of the skills I would eventually require.

--- The_Case_of_Charles_Dexter_Ward_The_H.P._Lovecraft_Wiki_Fandom_abd28ac330.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L339
Horror historian Les Daniels called The Case of Charles Dexter Ward Lovecraft's "finest novel". E. F. Bleiler noted that the short novel, "despite its being strangely tired and routine, has interesting concepts and good moments". Baird Searles found that "HPL's great knowledge of New England history provides a convincing background" for the story. Douglas Robillard stated Lovecraft's negative assessment of The Case of Charles Dexter Ward was "too harsh; this is one of his finest works". Cthulhu Mythos[] Charles Dexter Ward contains the first mention of the Cthulhu Mythos entity Yog-Sothoth, who appears repeatedly as an element in an incantation. Joseph Curwen is the owner of a copy of the Necronomicon (disguised as a book labelled Qanoon-e-Islam) and there are hints of cult activities in a fishing village that refer obliquely to the events narrated in "The Festival". The story also contains references to the Dream Cycle: Dr. Willett notices the "Sign of Koth" chiselled above a doorway, and remembers his friend Randolph Carter drawing the sign and explaining its powers and meaning. First appearance of the Dragon's Head and Dragon's Tail signs.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L343
Joseph Curwen is the owner of a copy of the Necronomicon (disguised as a book labelled Qanoon-e-Islam) and there are hints of cult activities in a fishing village that refer obliquely to the events narrated in "The Festival". --- The_Cthulhu_Mythos_An_Annotated_Bibliography_ce0a686327 [The Cthulhu Mythos_ An Annotated Bibliography_1.txt].txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L109
This bibliography is not intended to assert that any particular story is or is not a "Mythos" story. For our current purposes, a Mythos story is simply any work that shares some amount of fictional background lore with Lovecraft's primary writings. There are several submythos or story clusters that have a life of their own: Bloch's Egyptian Mythos and Howard's Hyborian Age stories, for example. Within Lovecraft's own writing, there are major clusters based around his fictional New England settings of Arkham etc; the elder beings such as Cthulhu, Yog-Sothoth, etc; and dreamland. These overlap in various places to varying degrees, and I would not exclude a story from this Guide simply because it is primarily a dreamland story, for example. HPL seemed to enjoy building links between different branches of his work, so there is no point in us erecting artificial barriers between them. The following entry from the H. P. Lovecraft section shows the general layout of the bibliography entries: Festival - The Festival, in Dagon and Other Macabre Tales. Narrator: nameless.

[2] The Key L147
In the Guide, this story is referred to as HPL Festival. Narrator: For most stories, the name of the narrator or the main protagonist is identified. In the case of first-person stories, the narrator's name is not always identified in the story. References: Terms that occur in the story and are indexed in the Guide. Key terms are highlighted in bold. A "key term" is one that occurs in more than one story, and is either unique to the Mythos, or became inducted into the Mythos in an interesting way. Looking at the key terms will give you an idea what eldritch threads tend to connect the story into the larger web of Mythos works. In some cases, it is not easy to establish whether an occult volume referred to in one of these stories is real, or a fictional embelllishment. A few real works of traditional occultism and demonology are referred to, and I have generally not highlighted these as key terms. Hyperlinks: The various terms are hyperlinked so you can click them to be taken to the article about that term.

[1] Yog L39
P. Lovecraft and his circle of friends and correspondents. Some notes are also included about earlier stories that influenced Lovecraft and his pals. I should hasten to add that later authors are omitted purely to limit the size of this index. I do not mean to imply any dubious standard of canonicity that enshrines the first generation of writers. Format of the Entries The majority of the book presents terms in alphabetical order. The following is a typical entry: Nameless Cults HPL Aeons copies in late 19th century rare 269, suppression of original Dusseldorf edition (1839) and Bridewell translation (1845) 269, expurgated reprint by Golden Goblin Press (1909) 269, resemblance of ideographs in Nameless Cults to scroll of T'yog 271. HH Guardian 'criminally expurgated later (1909) edition' 288. REH Black 56; Children 151; Roof 197; Untitled 37. See also: Black Book, Unaussprechlichen Kulten. In this entry, Nameless Cults is the term being indexed. HPL, HH, and REH are abbreviations for the authors H. P. Lovecraft, Henry Hasse, and Robert E. Howard. Aeons, Guardian, Black, and so on are abbreviations for story names. To determine the meaning of any particular author abbreviation or story abbreviation, refer to the Bibliography that follows this introduction.

Plot summary[] In the isolated, desolate, decrepit village of Dunwich, Wilbur Whateley is the hideous son of Lavinia Whateley, a deformed and unstable albino mother, and an unknown father (alluded to in passing by mad Old Whateley, as "Yog-Sothoth"). Strange events surround his birth and precocious development. Wilbur matures at an abnormal rate, reaching manhood within a decade. Locals shun him and his family, and animals fear and despise him (due to his odor). All the while, his sorcerer grandfather indoctrinates him into certain dark rituals and the study of witchcraft.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L325
Wilbur matures at an abnormal rate, reaching manhood within a decade. Locals shun him and his family, and animals fear and despise him (due to his odor). All the while, his sorcerer grandfather indoctrinates him into certain dark rituals and the study of witchcraft. Various locals grow suspicious after Old Whateley buys more and more cattle, yet the number of his herd never increases, and the cattle in his field become mysteriously afflicted with severe open wounds. Wilbur and his grandfather have sequestered an unseen presence at their farmhouse; this being is connected somehow to Yog-Sothoth. Year by year, this unseen entity grows to monstrous proportions, requiring the two men to make frequent modifications to their residence. People begin to notice a trend of cattle mysteriously disappearing. Wilbur's grandfather dies. His mother disappears soon afterwards. The colossal entity eventually occupies the whole interior of the farmhouse.

Isolated among strange influences, Lavinia was fond of wild and grandiose day-dreams and singular occupations. " Elsewhere, she is called "slatternly [and] crinkly-haired". [1] The Gate L263
They then discover why, as they find both Mad Dan and his wife petrified inside, Dan tied to a chair with a leather whip, and Rose strangely smug in her final moments. The pair find Dan's diary on the table, which tells the story in great detail. Dan is the decedent of a certain Nicolas Van Kauran, a wizard once burned at the stake, though his copy of the Book of Eibon survived, and was passed down through the generations. Dan continues to perform ancient rites into the present, including sacrificing to Shubb-Niggurath, and complaining that the villagers "always prevent my doing the Great Rite that would open the gate." Rose also does not participate in his ceremonies, much to his complaints, and when Wheeler arrives and Dan notices their flirting, he contrives a horrible revenge. After several months of study (during which he discards ideas like, "the emanation of with," or "The Green Decay") Morris finds a weapon with a poetic flourish: a potion to induce petrification, once used for murder by another ancestor. Admitting it has more to do with science than magic, he constructs a secret laboratory in the cave, testing his formulas on passing animals.

"In telling him of the pleasure I had had in rereading it, I suggested a sequel to account for [protagonist] Randolph Carter 's doings after his disappearance." After convincing an apparently reluctant Lovecraft to agree to collaborate on such a sequel, Price wrote a 6,000-word draft in August 1932; in April 1933, Lovecraft produced a 14,000-word version that left unchanged, by Price's estimate, "fewer than fifty of my original words," though An H. P. Lovecraft Encyclopedia Thus, many of the central ideas of the story like 'Umr at-Tawil theosophy , and the occult. Even the quote from the Necronomicon is mainly by Price in outline, though put in more Lovecraftian language. ( EXP An H. P. Lovecraft Encyclopedia ) The sub-plot about Yaddith was entirely Lovecraft's idea, however. In any case, Price was pleased with the result, writing that Lovecraft "was right of course in discarding all but the basic outline. I could only marvel that he had made so much of my inadequate and bungling start."

[2] The Key L151
The story appeared under both authors' bylines in the July 1934 issue of Weird Tales ; Price's draft was published as "The Lord of Illusion" in Crypt of Cthulhu No. 10 in 1982. Synopsis At a gathering to decide the fate of Randolph Carter's estate, which has been held in trust since his disappearance, the mysterious Swami Chandraputra , who wears curious mittens and enveloping robes, tells Carter's acquaintances of his ultimate fate. He explains that the key took Carter to a type of higher dimension. There, Carter, on an ill-defined mission (or out of sheer curiosity), travelled strange sections of the cosmos by first meeting with 'Umr at-Tawil, a dangerous being warned of in the Necronomicon , saying that those who deal with it never return. 'Umr at-Tawil offers Carter a chance to plunge deeper into the cosmos; Carter thus perceives the true nature of the universe before passing through the "Ultimate Gate."

Mythos Connections The artefact that emerges from the Antarctic ice, a "crackle-skinned sphere of pitted brown metal" 40 feet in diameter, is called the Furnace of Yeb. Depicted in the Necronomicon--"circa 738 A. D." --it's "the Elder engine that’s supposed to clear the Earth." Yeb is described in the story as one of the greatest of the Old Ones. The offspring of Yog-Sothoth and Shub-Niggurath , father to Tsathoggua . In ancient times, he was worshipped in underground shrines all over the world. In Rome, Luxor, Petra——even Teotihuacan. Two years ago when they uncovered the lost city of Irem in the Middle East, they found a cave shrine dedicated to Yeb. In the Irem shrine, the CEET found a "basalt wall tablet... the only complete surviving text of the Black Litany that is identified with Yeb." It describes something associated with Yeb called the Black Fire.

[3] Yog-Sothoth L347
His first appearance in print, however, was in H. P. Lovecraft's story The Whisperer in Darkness, written in 1930 and published in the August 1931 Weird Tales. Lovecraft mentioned Tsathoggua in nine stories, not counting the unfinished fragment that would later become The Lurker at the Threshold. This makes it one of the most oft-mentioned Mythos deities in Lovecraft's fiction, tied with Yog-Sothoth and losing only to Nyarlathotep (ten stories), Cthulhu and Shub-Niggurath (eleven stories each). Of these, Tsathoggua is the only one not created by Lovecraft himself. Like Shub-Niggurath, however, Tsathoggua never appears physically in Lovecraft's stories, except for a possible appearance disguised as a wax sculpture in "The Horror in the Museum".

[7] Yog-Sothoth L453
The Star Vampires might also be associated with Tsathoggua, given that the incantation to summon them mentions "bufoniformis Sadoquae", i. e. toad-like Tsathoggua. (CIRCLE: "The Shambler from the Stars") At least one source identifies Tsathoggua as one of the many Great Old Ones who rebelled against the Elder Gods, leading the earth elementals alongside Yog-Sothoth (AWD: "The Sandwin Compact"). The Book of Eibon suggests that some sort of rivalry exists between the elemental beings of earth and air, explaining the enmity between the Voormis, who worship Tsathoggua, and the Gnophkehs, who worship Rhan-Tegoth (EXP: "The Scroll of Morloc").

[3] Yog L59
C. /December 8, 1931 Occupation High-Priest of Shub-Niggurath Species Human First appearance HPL Out of the Aeons Created by H. P. Lovecraft Hazel Heald T'yog is a fictional character from H. P. Lovecraft and Hazel Heald 's story " Out of the Aeons ", an ancient priest turned into a mummy by the sight of Ghatanothoa . T'yog first appeared in the April 1935 issue of Weird Tales High-Priest of Shub-Niggurath Von Junzt Nameless Cults --a book invented by Lovecraft's friend Robert E. Howard in the short story " The Children of the Night ". In "Out of the Aeons", the book recounts a myth from the lost continent of Mu , which flourished in what is now the Pacific Ocean some 200,000 years ago.

[4] Yog L95
In Mu there was said to be a land called K'naa , dominated by the priesthood of Ghatanothoa, an alien entity living beneath the sacred mountain Yaddith-Gho , and kept quiescent by annual human sacrifice. T'yog, Von Junzt relates, was the High-Priest of Shub-Niggurath , the "guardian of the copper temple of the Goat with a Thousand Young"; the cleric, a "heretic" noted for his "skill and zeal", had "thought long on the powers of the various gods, and had had strange dreams and revelations touching the life of this and earlier worlds." He resented the power of the cult of Ghatanothoa, and believed that with his own god, along with the twin gods Nug and Yeb , and the Serpent-god Yig , were "ready to take sides with man against the tyranny and presumption of Ghatanothoa."

[6] Yog L109
He resented the power of the cult of Ghatanothoa, and believed that with his own god, along with the twin gods Nug and Yeb , and the Serpent-god Yig , were "ready to take sides with man against the tyranny and presumption of Ghatanothoa." T'yog prepared to confront Ghatanothoa in his "alien-angled citadel of Cyclopean stone" by creating a scroll, written in "hieratic Naacal " on pthagon membrane (the inner skin of a yakith-lizard ) and encased in "a carven cylinder of lagh metal " brought from Yuggoth , that would neutralize the power of the Daemon-God. On the Day of the Sky-Flames in the Year of the Red Moon--estimated to be 173,148 B. C. by Von Junzt--the High-Priest set forth , with the blessings of K'naa's King Thabon and the hopes of the people, to "confront the shocking devil-entity in its lair".

[7] Yog L137
On the Day of the Sky-Flames in the Year of the Red Moon--estimated to be 173,148 B. C. by Von Junzt--the High-Priest set forth , with the blessings of K'naa's King Thabon and the hopes of the people, to "confront the shocking devil-entity in its lair". Unbeknownst to T'yog, however, the High-Priest of Ghatanothoa, Imash-Mo , had switched his scroll with an ineffectual facsimile, rendering him powerless against the Devil-God. Rather than breaking the power of Ghatanothoa, he was instead petrified by the sight of the horrific entity, transformed into a living mummy. In that immobile form, T'yog survived through the aeons as Mu sank beneath the waves of the Pacific.

The Eridanus Mummy T'yog's mummy was found on May 11, 1878, when the freighter Eridanus , en route from New Zealand to Chile, encountered a "new island unmarked on any chart", "suddenly upheaved from the Pacific's floor." In a "massive stone crypt" on the island, formed of "prehistoric Cyclopean masonry", Capt. Charles Weatherbee found the "ghastly, inexplicable mummy", which he brought back to Valparaiso. There it was acquired by Boston's Cabot Museum of Archaeology, which put it on display in November 1879. The mummy is described as a medium-sized man of unknown race...

[10] Yog L175
Rags of some peculiar fabric, with suggestions of unknown designs, still clung to the object. The mummy had been on display for half a century, the Cabot Museum 's "chief attraction and most impenetrable mystery", when a sensational article in the Boston Pillar , dated April 5, 1931, brought it to first local and then global attention. Under the attention of throngs of visitors--including latter-day worshippers of Ghatanothoa, one of whom, Nagob , carries the true scroll of T'yog--the mummy is seen to undergo changes, as "the half-stony, half-leathery fibres seemed to be gradually relaxing, causing distinct variations in the angles of the limbs and in certain details of the fear-twisted facial expression." Most notably, the mummy's eyes slightly open, with "a thin crescent of cornea being visible in either eye". (One visitor makes explicit the connection between the mummy and the legendary figure from Von Junzt's book: " "It tried to open its eyes! —T’yog tried to open his eyes and stare at me!"

[11] Yog L175
Most notably, the mummy's eyes slightly open, with "a thin crescent of cornea being visible in either eye". (One visitor makes explicit the connection between the mummy and the legendary figure from Von Junzt's book: " "It tried to open its eyes! —T’yog tried to open his eyes and stare at me!" shrieks a "Peruvian of Indian blood" who "suffered a strange hysterical or epileptic seizure in front of the mummy.") A series of disturbances at the museum climax on December 1, 1931, with the murder of a nightwatchman and the deaths of two intruders in front of the mummy, one of whom carries the true scroll.

[12] Yog L185
Most disturbingly, " its hellish bulging eyes had popped wide open ." Noting "the theory that scenes and objects become photographed on the retina of the eye in cases of death or coma," the narrator--curator Richard H. Johnson --sees the preserved image of Ghatanothoa in T'yog's eyes. Though it sends him into a faint, the image had already faded; he surmises it must have appeared with greater clarity when the eyes first opened, with power enough to kill one cultist from fright, and to petrify the one not protected by the scroll.


--- Ubbo-Sathla (Cthulhu Universalis).txt ---

[1] Yok-Zothoth L13
НАЗВАНИЕ: Ubbo-Sathla (Cthulhu Universalis) ИСТОЧНИК: Ubbo-Sathla The unbegotten source, a being who dwelt in the steaming fens of the new-made Earth, before the coming of Zhothaqquah or Yok-Zothoth or Kthulhut from the stars. Ubbo-Sathla was a formless mass without head or members, who lay vast and swollen and yeasty amid the vaporing slime . It sloughed from its oozy sides, in a slow, ceaseless wave, the grey, formless efts of the prime and the amoebic forms that were the archetypes of earthly life. There in the primal mire, Ubbo-Sathla also guarded the wisdom of the gods who died before the Earth was born, which was inscribed upon tablets of ultra-stellar stone.

Нелепая голова, без носа и подбородка, с выпученными глазами, ртом-щелью с толстыми губами, а вместо ушей — бахрома жабр, растущая по изгибам челюстей. Это был монстр, что надо, и достаточно уродливый, чтобы удовлетворить даже самого требовательного продюсера. Но все же он заставил меня улыбнуться. Было ясно, что Тед вложил в него много себя.

[3] Тот L57

Внимание хорошенькой девушки было в новинку в его жизни, и он не знал, куда деться. Это не должно было стать сюрпризом. Но только в тот момент я осознал, как плохо было бедному парню. Он с трудом сдерживался, чтобы не сбежать. Ив быстро поняла, в чем дело, и сделала все возможное, чтобы помочь ему справиться. Она удерживала его внимание на предмете разговора так, будто это было самое интересное в мире. И должен сказать, ее подход сработал. [5] Тот L157
Но когда через час я остановился перед его бунгало, то подумал, что проделал путь зря. Дом был темен, словно он внял моему совету и лег спать. Оно напоминало декорацию салуна в вестерне после большой драки. Лампы разбиты, стулья опрокинуты, обивка распорота. Ковер был пропитан водой и чем-то еще, похожим на кровь. А где же Тед и его дядя? По телефону Тед звучал довольно безумно, но достаточно ли он обезумел, чтобы напасть на дядю в убеждении, что тот — монстр, угрожающий женщине, которую он любит? Достаточно ли он обезумел, чтобы убить его, вытащить тело на пляж, закопать в песок или пустить дрейфовать по воде? Я не знал, и это было не мое дело выяснять. Я откопал телефон Теда из-под обломков и позвонил в полицию. Затем вышел на крыльцо ждать их. И там я увидел нечто, заставившее меня подумать, что, возможно, бедный старина Тед вовсе не был таким уж безумным. Кто-то прошел этим путем до меня, оставляя следы воды и крови с промокшего ковра на деревянном настиле. Но этот кто-то не был Тедом.


--- United States of America.txt ---

[1] The Gate L145
In 1931 he returned to Charleston; visited Savannah, Georgia; and spent considerable time in St. Augustine, Key West, and other Florida towns. A trip that started in May 1932 took him to Tennessee, Mississippi, and Alabama, and allowed him to visit E. Hoffman Price in New Orleans In the summers of 1934 and 1935, Lovecraft had extended stays with R. H. Barlow in DeLand, Florida, visiting or revisiting several cities on the way to and from those visits. America in Lovecraft's Fiction While Lovecraft famously used New England as a backdrop for his horror fiction, leading to the dubbing of a region in northeastern Massachusetts as Lovecraft Country , he also set stories in several other far-flung states, including New York, both the city He Cool Air The Horror at Red Hook ") and the state The Lurking Fear Beyond the Wall of Sleep The Diary of Alonzo Typer Louisiana The Call of Cthulhu Through the Gate of the Silver Key "); Florida (" The Statement of Randolph Carter "); Kentucky (" The Beast in the Cave "), Oklahoma (" The Mound The Curse of Yig "); and Missouri (" Medusa's Coil Correspondents Lovecraft maintained a voluminous correspondence with pen pals across the country, including Clark Ashton Smith and Henry Kuttner in California Robert E. Howard in Texas, August Derleth and Robert Bloch in Wisconsin Fritz Leiber in Chicago, and Frank Belknap Long in New York City . When these writers contributed their own work to the Cthulhu Mythos , they often used local settings that further broadened the geographic scope of the Mythos.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Weak ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:34:46 СИМВОЛОВ: 624 Weak Full story online here Author Peter A. Worthy Language English Publication date December 1997 Weak " is a Cthulhu Mythos piece by author Peter A. Worthy . It would appear to be a set of alternative lyrics written to be sung to British rock band Skunk Anansie's 1996 single "Weak." Synopsis The poem consists of six short verses which namecheck a number of entities and locations associated with the Cthulhu Mythos, including Yog-Sothoth Cthulhu , and the Deep Ones "Weak" was first published in the online zine Nightscapes in December 1997, and later appeared in print in Cthulhu Cultus in April the following year.

--- Wilbur Whateley Waiting.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L67
After several years on his old homestead contemplating what to do, he stumbles across a cave, inside of which is a door. The door is covered in arcane symbols which he recognises from his old grimoires , and the story ends with Wilbur opening the door and preparing to begin again. As for Prinn, he finds that he has the correct incantation after all and awakens Rhan-Tegoth, which kills him and goes back to sleep after no blood sacrifices are forthcoming. Characters Wilbur Whateley , the semi-human son of Yog-Sothoth , who is dedicated to bringing the Earth into his father's hands. Ezekiel Prinn , an aging but dedicated, if somewhat ill-informed, occultist. Rhan-Tegoth , a Great Old One which will summon the rest of its kind if successfully unleashed. "Wilbur Whateley Waiting" was first published in the fanzine Revelations from Yuggoth in November 1987. It later appeared in the anthologies The Dunwich Cycle: Where the Old Gods Wait (November 1995) and Blasphemies & Revelations (November 2008). --- Wilbur Whateley.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L29
НАЗВАНИЕ: Wilbur Whateley ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:34:58 СИМВОЛОВ: 5899 Wilbur Whateley Born February 2nd, 1913 Died August 3, 1928 Relatives Old Whateley (maternal grandfather) Lavinia Whateley (mother) Yog-Sothoth (father) Dunwich Horror (twin brother) Cthulhu (half-nephew) First appearance HPL The Dunwich Horror Appearances EXP Demonbane Wilbur Whateley Waiting "The City at the Two Magnetic Poles" Created by H. P. Lovecraft Wilbur Whateley is a fictional character created by H. P. Lovecraft for his short story " The Dunwich Horror Background In the rural town of Dunwich, Massachusetts on February 2, 1913 at 5 a. m. , Lavinia Whateley gave birth to a son named Wilbur Whateley. The date of his birth is noted for the night before the hills rumbled and dogs barked incessantly. Dogs continued to show an instinctual hatred for him for the remainder of his life.

[2] Yog-Sothoth L97
At a young age he takes to wearing very concealing clothes. He also has a revolting odor about his person, a defining characteristic of the Great Old Ones . Wilbur's voice is distinctive for its "Strange, resonant fashion which hinted at sound-producing organs unlike the run of mankind's". This presumably allows him to speak the language of the Great Old Ones. At 15 years he had grown to 9 feet tall and showed no sign of stopping. Prior to his grandfather’s death he left him with the responsibility of raising his twin as well as ensuring he opens the gates to Yog-Sothoth . He could only accomplish this by finding the summoning ritual on of the Necronomicon . He then travelled to the Miskatonic , Cambridge, and Widener libraries in search of a complete version of this book. They all, under the guidance of Dr. Armitage , denied him access. He was then forced to return to Miskatonic University to steal their copy. This attempt ultimately proves his downfall, when a watchdog savagely kills him. It succeeded solely because Whateley's revolver failed to fire.

[3] Yog-Sothoth L147
Immediately afterward his corpse disintegrated into a sticky white mass, apparently having no true skeletal structure. Out the window a swarm of Whippoorwills were heard shrieking in anticipation for his soul. They soon fled after witnessing their intended prey. Afterwards, Wilbur Whateley's journal and the contents of his library were transported to Miskatonic University to be studied. ( HPL The Dunwich Horror Film Adaptations Wilbur Whateley was a central character in the 1970 film The Dunwich Horror . His depiction in the film differs greatly from the story, in that he is depicted as a normal-looking human with none of the unnatural characteristics described in Lovecraft's tale, except that he does possess the supernatural ability to influence people's minds, particularly that of his intended victim, Nancy Wagner, whom he intends to impregnate with the child of Yog-Sothoth. Wilbur was played by actor Dean Stockwell , who would later play Armitage in the 2008 remake . In the remake, Wilbur was played by Jeffrey Combs In the Demonbane Mythos Wilbur Whateley appears as an antagonist in the Demonbane series by Nitroplus, sharing many similarities with Lovecraft's original depiction. Daijuuji Kurou had an encounter with Wilbur Whateley at Miskatonic University. On that day, Kurou was given permission to view the Necronomicon in the secret library but was interrupted by Wilbur, who wanted to steal the grimoire for himself.

--- Winter Tide.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L291
The Hall School, which is mentioned in "The Thing on the Doorstep," is presented as Miskatonic's all-female sister college, kept at "a well-chaperoned distance on the far side of Kingsport." It is less possessive of its arcane literature than Miskatonic. It appears as "a series of low-slung brick buildings with none of Miskatonic’s flourishes." Aeonism Winter Tide expands on The Litany of Earth 's presentation of Mythos religion not as a depraved cult but as a sincere expression of spirituality, referred to by practitioners as Aeonism. Aphra Marsh prays to a pantheon of Lovecraftian entities, including " Dagon , guardian of waters, steadfast"; " Hydra , defender of waters, fierce"; " Cthulhu , bringer of life and death, ever patient"; " Nyarlathotep , herald of knowledge"; " Yog-Sothoth , maker and keeper of gates"; " Azathoth , void and melody"; and, under a variant spelling, " Shub-Nigaroth , mother of fear." The "ostensibly nondenominational" campus church at Miskatonic is "extremely Christian," but has a "discreet" shrine in the back for Aeonist worshipers. Aphra describes it: A stone altar stood empty except for a single candle. If I let my eyes unfocus, the half-abstract carvings resolved into great tentacles reaching from the altar to enfold the little grotto. The artist, I realized, had placed those who knelt there within the god’s embrace, while making the god invisible to any who did not know to look.

НАЗВАНИЕ: Worm that Walks ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:35:09 СИМВОЛОВ: 1052 Worm that Walks First appearance EXP Shadows of Yog-Sothoth , Chapter 5: "The Worm That Walks" Created by Sandy Petersen The Worm that Walks is a fictional entity created by Sandy Petersen for Chaosium Call of Cthulhu horror role-playing game. He bent in greedy haste to retrieve them and Bran Mak Morn rode westward like a flying ghost in the night.

--- Worse Things Waiting.txt ---

[3] The Gate L65
It was originally published in 1980 as Satan's Seductress (Carlyle Books), and released under McNaughton's preferred title in 2000 by Wildside Press. It is a sequel to 1978's Downward to Darkness (aka Satan's Mistress ). Like its predecessor, Worse Things Waiting combines McNaughton's trademark black humour, plentiful gore and pervasive sexuality. The title comes from a quote from A. C. Swinburne that serves as the book's epigraph: At the door of life, by the gate of breath, There are worse things waiting for men than death. Synopsis Four years after the events of Downward to Darkness , Amy Miniter has returned to Mt. Tabor, Connecticut--and has been identified by local Satanist Howard Ashcroft as a likely vessel for the reincarnation of 19th century witch Mirdath Hodgson. Meanwhile, hack writer Martin Paige has come to town to do a true crime story about the Mt. Tabor massacre--and ends up falling in love with Amy and risking everything to thwart Mirdath's scheme.

--- Xothic Legend Cycle.txt ---

[12] Yog L301
Zanthu , the high priest of Ythogtha, plots to depose the cult of Ghatanothoa after his priests outlawed all other religions in Mu . The cult of Ghatanothoa was the dominant religion in Mu following the defeat of T'yog , high priest of Shub-Niggurath , who had sought to vanquish the tyranny of Ghatanothoa forever. Zanthu had hoped to oust Ghatanothoa's cult by freeing the god Ythogtha from the Abyss of Yhe , where the Elder Gods had imprisoned him. This act of blasphemy did not go unnoticed by the Elder Gods, who destroyed Mu and sank it beneath the sea.

--- Yaldabaoth.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L101
Other times the Demiurge is simply shown as an old and dour man, also having saturnal implications and later assimilating the imagery of the God of the religions of Judaic origin. This is mainly due to the neo-Gnostic currents considering that the God of monotheism is just another identity that the demiurge adopts to attract followers. Conceptual information and role Despite not being a god created by the Lovecraft Circle, its integration into the bestiaries of the Mythos is undoubtedly due to its cosmic character. It is not uncommon for Yaldabaoth to be assimilated to Azathoth or Yog-Sothoth , and it is also typical for him to be associated with Nyarlathotep , since Samael, a name associated with the Demiurge, is one of the many identities that he adopts. In Popular Culture A version of Yaldabaoth was incorporated into the SCP Foundation online writing community as a destructive entity which feeds upon deities and stars, then exhales life.

--- Yibb-Tstll.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L67

Brian Lumley EXP Rising with Surtsey Yibb-Tstll The Patient One ) is a fictional entity in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos . The character was originally created by Brian Lumley for his short story " Rising with Surtsey Background Yibb-Tstll is an obscure god, said to watch at the center of all time as the universe revolves. Because of this insight, only Yog-Sothoth is said to be wiser. Its blood, The Black , is a weapon which takes the form of black snowflakes that stick to and smother a victim. The god's touch causes an instant change in the person affected, this change is usually fatal but occasionally brings some benefit. Yibb-Tstll is sometimes described as an immobile, dark, tentacled entity with a pulpy, alien head, detached eyes, and large bat wings under which countless Night-gaunts suck black milk from its innumerable breasts.

The supervillain Doctor Doom used the power of the ninth Makluan Ring to open wormholes to other dimensions, summoning Yogthulu in hopes of reuniting with his family. Doctor Doom kidnapped the superhero Iron Man, along with his father Howard Stark and his adversary the Mandarin, planning to exchange those "three pure souls" for Yogthulu to bring back his family; however, Yogthulu was able to sense impurity in one of the souls, calling off the deal. НАЗВАНИЕ: Young Goodwife Doten ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:35:25 СИМВОЛОВ: 1623 Young Goodwife Doten Author Robert M. Price Country United States Language English Genre(s) Horror Publication date September 1995 Young Goodwife Doten " is a short story by American author Robert M. Price . It is an expansion on events referenced in Thaumaturgical Prodigies in the New-England Canaan , a fictional book which appeared in The Lurker at the Threshold Synopsis A young couple living near Arkham in what will one day become New England find that all of their attempts to have children result in stillbirth. In desperation they turn to a reclusive old woman who lives in the nearby woods, and is rumoured to possess arcane knowledge; after a visit to the woman, and coupling with what she believes to be an angel of heaven, the wife indeed becomes pregnant. However, on the day of the birth the midwife runs in terror from the abomination which she sees brought into the world. It is quickly put to death, and the young couple burnt for witchcraft.


--- Ythogtha.txt ---

[1] Yog-Sothoth L19
НАЗВАНИЕ: Ythogtha ИСТОЧНИК: ДАТА: 2026-06-15 03:35:24 СИМВОЛОВ: 1077 Ythogtha Also known as The Thing in the Pit The Abomination in the Abyss Relatives Yog-Sothoth (great-grandparent) Shub-Niggurath (great-grandparent) Nug (grandparent) Cthulhu (father) Idh-yaa (mother) Ghatanothoa (sibling) Zoth-Ommog (sibling) Cthylla (sibling) Affiliations Great Old Ones First appearance EXP Out of the Ages Appearances EXP The Thing in the Pit Created by Lin Carter Ythogtha is a Great Old One in the expanded Cthulhu Mythos . The character was created by Lin Carter for his Xothic Legend Cycle Description Ythogtha is the second son of Cthulhu who resembles a gigantic, humanoid frog or Deep One , with but a single, huge eye in the center of his forehead like a cyclops. A dense mane and a beard of writhing tentacles grows from his head. Ythogtha is incredibly large; when the sorcerer-priest Zanthu attempts to free Ythogtha from his prison, he mistakes his god's clawed, slimy fingertips for mountainous heads.

--- Zoog.txt ---

[1] The Gate L65
Randolph Carter enlisted the aid of the Zoogs during his quest for Kadath They are small and curious, and usually unseen. One sees their weird eyes long before one can discern their slippery brown outlines. The Zoogs' speech consists of fluttering sounds. Although they eat mostly fungi, they are not above occasionally eating animals or visiting dreamers. The zoogs make a wine from the fermented sap of a moon-tree (a tree grown from a seed dropped down by someone on the Moon of the Dreamlands). The Zoogs dwell in the enchanted wood, just past the Gate of Deeper Slumber in the world of dream. They cannot travel far outside the world of dream, but range freely over the nearer parts of dreamland. One of their villages is near an old circle of mossy stone, where elder beings danced and sacrificed. The Zoogs fear and shun a stone slab set with a huge iron ring. This slab if opened reveals a path that leads down to the realm where the Gugs were banished in the underworld of the Dreamlands. The Zoog Council of Sages at one point recognized Randolph Carter as an old ally.

--- the_Twentieth_Century's_greatest_practitioner_of_the_classic_horror_tale_f6337ee4b8.txt ---

[2] Yog-Sothoth L93
All my stories, unconnected as they may be, are based on the fundamental lore or legend that this world was inhabited at one time by another race, who in practicing black magic, lost their foothold and were expelled, yet live on outside, ever ready to take possession of this earth again (de Camp, 271). It has been proven that the above, long believed to be an actual quote from Lovecraft, was merely a fabrication of August Derleth used to support his interpretation of the author's conceptions. Lovecraft's major creature creations include the Elder God characters "Cthulhu," "Yog-Sothoth," "Nyarlathotep" and the alien "Yuggothites." His fictitious works of mythic lore and sorcery include the Necronomicon, "a book of portentous spells for summoning dire entities from other worlds and dimensions" (de Camp, 166-67) by "the mad Arab Abdul Alhazred," and The Pnakotic Manuscripts. His correspondents, fans, and later Mythos writers have added to this pseudobiblia.

--- Аспекты Эвокации.txt ---

[1] Тот L171
Заключительное эссе, Вызывание Йог - Сотот а (первоначально написанное для журнала Эзотерическ ого Орден а Дагона ) - это попытка собрать 6 воедино теоретическую модель, связанную с сущностями мифов , земными огнями и другими факторами. В то время, когда я писал эту книгу, я очень любил создавать теоретические модели, прежде чем приступать к практическим проектам. В нек отором смысле, специализироваться на методах вызывания меня побудил тот факт, что в то время я не встречал много полезной информации об этой магической практике. Потому-то на Гаити, когда неизлечимо больной вдруг неожиданно выздоравливает, говорят: "Самеди отказался ему рыть могилу". Однако не особо много смельчаков обращается к Барону Самеди с просьбами.

--- Безликий Король.txt ---

[1] Тот L43
Создателю маски Король явился как невидимая разумная сущность, способная принимать неопределенную форму, взгляд на которую приводит к потере памяти и, в некоторых случаях, к убеждению человека, что он сам и есть "Безликий Король". Истинный облик Короля неизвестен. Культ Ро́єда́ считает, что после Великого Бедствия и поражения тело божества было разрушено и Король теперь существует как бесформенное, постоянно меняющееся существо из чистой мысли и воли, однако другие считают, что Король сохранил свой физический облик, но неизвестно, как он выглядит, поскольку попасть в тюрьму Короля нельзя и, скорее всего, тот, кому это удастся, сразу будет захвачен Королем, прежде чем успеет что-либо рассказать. Учёные из Истахра раскрывают, что Король может манипулировала своим истинным обликом, увеличивая и уменьшая его и изменяя черты. Из-за этого освобожденный Король может в один момент стать гигантским колоссом, шагающим по городу, а в другой- гуманоидом человеческого роста, скрывающим облик под рваными одеждами.

[2] Тот L67

Исследование происхождения Объекта-77 выявило ряд древних текстов, на всех из которых изображена похожая фигура, окрашенная в тот же желтый цвет. Исследования дома археолога выявили коллекцию писем, по-видимому, отправленных разными людьми, в которых описывается непонятная фигура, одетая в желтое, которая морально истязала их, заставляя создавать произведения искусства, связанные с ним. [3] Той L195
Символ Дефтанеха — Ключ. Имея ключи от некоторых пространств, Он может посылать вещие сны. Очень любит кровь. С удовольствием и радостью примет, коли ты принесёшь в жертву любое существо, кое не вызывает в тебе ни любви, ни ненависти, ни сострадания. Аззарейх. В прошлом эоне процветал Культ Насекомых. Самым кровавым и жестоким был Культ Паука. Жрица Культа Паука по имени Кара’лея ("Чёрная душа") увела за собой в мир иной целый народ и за эту заслугу получила ранг Басуроподобной и стала той, кого знают под именем Аззарейх. Аззарейх почитают как тёмную королеву-паучиху, прядущую желания разрушения, помогающую сновидцам и новоумершим. Она выглядит подобно Пазузу, но женского рода и в маске паука. Тождественна греческой Арахне. Её можно призвать для того, чтобы Она накачивала тебя силой, необходимой для осознанных снов, а перед смертью можно договориться с Ней, чтобы после смерти Она помогла тебе оклематься в новом качестве. Но может с Ней таким образом общаться лишь сильный Яту, весьма отличившийся своими заслугами, ибо ни от кого боле поклоненья Она не приемлет, и ежели кто до Неё достучится, тот будет рассоздан.

--- Возрождение Дагона.txt ---

[1] Тот L23
Там говорится, что Ктулху, Сущность водной стихии "был более Велик, нежели Дагон, так что Дагон и Его Глубоководные служили Ему". Тем не менее, наличие упоминаний о Дагоне в произведениях Лавкрафта, всегда будоражило умы исследователей и даже простых энтузиастов. Например, и Роберт М. Прайс и Уилл Мюррей, настаивают на том, что Образ Дагона стал неким прототипом для последующего за ним Образа Ктулху. Господин Прайс, например, выдвинул идею, что Имя Дагона, взятое из Ветхого Завета, использовалось членами тайного культа, только для того, что бы скрыть свое поклонение Неведомому Ктулху(1). Мюррей же в свою очередь, не смотря на то, что Лавкрафт позиционировал Орден как "рассредоточенный, псевдо-языческий орден, который пришел из Запада, век тому назад", предполагает, что "поклонение Дагону часто упоминается в Библии, хотя и вскользь", и что это, скорее всего, именно тот источник, из которого Лавкрафт и почерпнул идею(2). Пожалуй, разгадка всего этого, находится в повести "Тень над Инстмутом", где главный информатор тайного городского культа, престарелый, наполовину безумный Задок Ален, сообщает следующее: "Ярость Яхве. Я был маленьким мальчиком, но то, что тогда видел и слышал, никогда не изгладится из моей памяти: Дагон и Ашторет, Велиар и Вельзевул, Золотой телец, ханаанские и филистимлянские идолы, вавилонские мерзости... Мене, текел, фарес..." В этом небольшом отрывке поднимаются темы, которые всегда будоражили сознание западного человека, в том виде, в котором они преподносятся в библейской литературе.
